title.en: Volume 307 Biographies 66: Qiao Weiyue, Wang Zhi, Zhang Yong, Dong Yan, Wei Tingshi, Lu Yan, Song Tuan, Ling Ce, Yang Tan, Chen Shiqing, Li Ruozhuo, Chen Zhiwei
title.raw: 卷三百〇七 列傳第六十六 喬維岳 王陟 張雍 董儼 魏廷式 盧琰 宋摶 凌策 楊覃 陳世卿 李若拙 陳知微 Volume 307 Biographies 66: Qiao Weiyue, Wang Zhi, Zhang Yong, Dong Yan, Wei Tingshi, Lu Yan, Song Tuan, Ling Ce, Yang Tan, Chen Shiqing, Li Ruozhuo, Chen Zhiwei

sentences.zh: 喬維岳

translations.literal: Qiao Weiyue
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Weiyue

sentences.zh: 喬維岳，字伯周，陳州南頓人。

translations.literal: Qiao Weiyue, courtesy name Bozhou, was a native of Nandun in Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Weiyue, whose courtesy name was Bozhou, came from Nandun in Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 治《三傳》。

translations.literal: He studied the Three Commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: He specialized in the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初登第，授太湖主簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande of Zhou, he passed the examinations and was appointed registrar of Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xiande era of the Later Zhou, he passed the civil service examinations and was appointed registrar of Taihu County.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷平輿令。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to magistrate of Pingyu.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he was transferred to serve as magistrate of Pingyu.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，右拾遺劉稹薦其才，擢為太子中舍、知高郵軍，通判揚州，徙常州。

translations.literal: During the Kaibao period, Right Remonstrator Liu Zhen recommended his talent; he was promoted to Gentleman of the Palace Library, put in charge of Gaoyou Military Prefecture, made vice commissioner of Yangzhou, and then transferred to Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao reign, Right Remonstrator Liu Zhen recommended him for his ability. He was promoted to Gentleman of the Palace Library, assigned to govern Gaoyou Military Prefecture, appointed vice commissioner of Yangzhou, and later transferred to Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 金陵平，又移昇州，改殿中丞。

translations.literal: When Jinling was pacified, he was again transferred to Sheng Prefecture and promoted to Vice Director in the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinling fell, he was reassigned to Sheng Prefecture and promoted to Vice Director in the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，徙襄州，俄丁內艱。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, he was transferred to Xiang Prefecture, and soon afterward entered mourning for a parent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he was posted to Xiang Prefecture, but before long he withdrew to observe mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 三年，陳洪進表納疆土，以其子文顯為泉州留後，朝廷議擇能臣關掌郡事，即起維岳為通判。

translations.literal: In the third year, Chen Hongjin submitted a memorial offering his territory; his son Wensian was made acting prefect of Quanzhou. The court deliberated on selecting a capable minister to oversee the prefectural administration, and Weiyue was immediately recalled from mourning to serve as vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Chen Hongjin offered his domain to the throne and his son Wensian was left as acting prefect of Quanzhou. The court sought a capable official to supervise the prefecture, and Weiyue was summoned from mourning to serve as vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會盜起仙遊莆田縣百丈鎮，眾十餘萬攻城，城中兵裁三千，勢甚危急。

translations.literal: It happened that bandits rose at Baizhang Town in Xianyou and Putian counties; more than a hundred thousand men attacked the city. The troops in the city numbered only three thousand, and the situation was extremely perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits then rose at Baizhang in Xianyou and Putian, and a force of more than a hundred thousand laid siege to the city. The garrison had barely three thousand men, and the danger was acute.

sentences.zh: 監軍何承矩、王文寶欲盡屠其民，燔府庫而遁。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the army He Chengju and Wang Wenbao wished to slaughter all the people, burn the government stores, and flee.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor He Chengju and Wang Wenbao proposed slaughtering the populace, burning the government warehouses, and escaping.

sentences.zh: 維岳挺然抗議，以為：「朝廷寄以綏遠，今惠澤未布，盜賊連結，反欲屠城，豈詔意哉！」

translations.literal: Weiyue stood forth and protested, saying: "The court has entrusted us with pacifying the distant regions. Now our gracious rule has not yet been spread abroad, bandits and robbers are joining together, and yet you wish to massacre the city—can this be the intent of the imperial edict!"
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue objected firmly, saying, "The court has charged us with bringing peace to this distant region. Our benevolent rule has scarcely been felt, the brigands are still gathering, and you would slaughter the city—how can that accord with the emperor's command?"

sentences.zh: 承矩等因復堅守，既而轉運使楊克讓率福州兵破賊，圍遂解，詔褒之。

translations.literal: Chengju and the others therefore resumed a stout defense; before long Transport Commissioner Yang Kerang led Fuzhou troops to defeat the bandits, and the siege was lifted. An edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Chengju and his colleagues thereupon held the city resolutely. Before long Transport Commissioner Yang Kerang led troops from Fuzhou to defeat the rebels and lift the siege, and the court issued an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 歸朝，為淮南轉運副使，遷右補闕，進為使。

translations.literal: On returning to court, he became Vice Transport Commissioner of Huainan, was promoted to Right Remonstrator, and then advanced to commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned to the capital he served as Vice Transport Commissioner for Huainan, was promoted to Right Remonstrator, and then became transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 淮河西流三十里曰山陽灣，水勢湍悍，運舟多罹覆溺。

translations.literal: Thirty li west along the Huai River is Shanyang Bay; the current is swift and fierce, and transport boats often suffer capsizing and drowning.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li west along the Huai lay Shanyang Bay, where the current ran swift and fierce and grain barges often capsized.

sentences.zh: 維岳規度開故沙河，自末口至淮陰磨盤口，凡四十里。

translations.literal: Weiyue surveyed and planned to reopen the old Sha River, from Mokou to Mopankou at Huaiyin, altogether forty li.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue surveyed the terrain and reopened the old Sha River from Mokou to Mopankou at Huaiyin, a distance of forty li in all.

sentences.zh: 又建安北至淮澨，總五堰，運舟所至，十經上下，其重載者皆卸糧而過，舟時壞失糧，綱卒緣此為奸，潛有侵盜。

translations.literal: Moreover, from north of Jian'an to the Huai estuary there were five weirs in all; wherever transport boats arrived they had to pass up and down ten times. Heavily laden boats all unloaded grain to pass through; boats were often damaged and grain lost, and transport guards took advantage of this to commit wrongdoing and secretly embezzle.
translations.idiomatic: From north of Jian'an to the Huai estuary there were five weirs in all. Every transport vessel had to be hauled up and down them repeatedly; heavily laden boats had to unload their grain to pass, boats were often damaged and grain lost, and the transport guards used the opportunity for fraud and secret theft.

sentences.zh: 維岳始命創二斗門於西河第三堰，二門相距逾五十步，覆以廈屋，設縣門積水，俟潮平乃泄之。

translations.literal: Weiyue first ordered the construction of two sluice gates at the third weir on the western river; the two gates were more than fifty paces apart, roofed with a covered hall, and equipped with hoist gates to store water, releasing it only when the tide was level.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue first had two sluice gates built at the third weir on the western channel, more than fifty paces apart, roofed with a covered structure and fitted with hoist gates to hold back the water until the tide had equalized.

sentences.zh: 建橫橋岸上，築土累石，以牢其址。

translations.literal: A transverse bridge was built on the bank, and earth and stone were piled to secure its foundations.
translations.idiomatic: A bridge was built across the bank, with earth and stone piled to secure its foundations.

sentences.zh: 自是弊盡革，而運舟往來無滯矣。

translations.literal: From this all abuses were completely reformed, and transport boats passed back and forth without delay.
translations.idiomatic: From that time all these abuses were eliminated, and transport vessels moved without obstruction.

sentences.zh: 嘗按部至泗州，慮獄，法掾誤斷囚至死。

translations.literal: Once when he was on an inspection tour and reached Si Prefecture, he reviewed the prisons; a legal clerk by error sentenced a prisoner to death.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while on an inspection tour in Si Prefecture, he reviewed the prisons and found that a legal clerk had mistakenly sentenced a prisoner to death.

sentences.zh: 維岳詰之，法掾俯伏，且泣曰：「有母年八十餘，今獲罪，則母不能活矣。」

translations.literal: Weiyue questioned him; the legal clerk prostrated himself and wept, saying: "I have a mother more than eighty years old. If I am punished now, my mother cannot live."
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue questioned him. The clerk prostrated himself in tears and said, "My mother is more than eighty years old. If I am punished now, she will not survive."

sentences.zh: 維岳憫之，因謂曰：「他日朝制按問，第云轉運使令處茲罪。」

translations.literal: Weiyue pitied him and therefore said to him: "When the court later investigates by inquiry, simply say the transport commissioner ordered this punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Moved to pity, Weiyue told him, "When the court later investigates, say only that the transport commissioner ordered this sentence."

sentences.zh: 卒如其言獲免，維岳坐贖金百二十斤，罷使職，權知楚州。

translations.literal: In the end, as he had said, the clerk was spared; Weiyue was sentenced to a fine of one hundred and twenty catties of copper, dismissed from his commissionership, and given provisional charge of Chu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the clerk was spared, just as he had been told. Weiyue was fined one hundred and twenty catties of copper, removed from his post as commissioner, and given provisional charge of Chu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 代還，為度支判官，轉本曹郎中，出為兩浙轉運使，歷知懷州、滄州。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, he served as a judge in the Bureau of Revenue, was transferred to Director of that bureau, went out as transport commissioner of the two Zhe circuits, and successively governed Huai and Cang Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When his tour ended he returned to court as a judge in the Bureau of Revenue, rose to director of that bureau, was posted as transport commissioner for the two Zhe circuits, and successively governed Huai and Cang Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 會考課京朝官，召還。

translations.literal: When the evaluation of capital officials was held, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital officials' performance review was held, he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 屬真宗以壽王尹京，精擇府僚，留為開封府推官，或言維岳在淮南，決獄不平允，左右有知其事者辨之，太宗特加賞異。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Zhenzong, as Prince of Shou, was administering the capital; the staff was carefully chosen, and Weiyue was retained as investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefectural government. Some said that while Weiyue was in Huainan his judicial decisions had not been fair; those at court who knew the facts explained, and Emperor Taizong especially marked him out for special favor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Zhenzong, as Prince of Shou, was administering the capital, and the staff was carefully selected. Weiyue was kept on as investigating officer of Kaifeng. Some claimed his judgments in Huainan had been unfair, but courtiers who knew the facts spoke in his defense, and Emperor Taizong singled him out for special favor.

sentences.zh: 儲闈建，兼左諭德，轉太常少卿。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent was established, he was concurrently Left Mentor, and was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent was formally installed, he was made concurrent Left Mentor and promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 京府事繁，維岳評處詳敏。

translations.literal: The capital prefecture's business was complex; Weiyue's assessments were detailed and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: The capital prefecture's caseload was heavy, but Weiyue handled its business with thoroughness and dispatch.

sentences.zh: 有王陟為司錄，真宗亦稱其明幹。

translations.literal: There was Wang Zhi as recorder; Emperor Zhenzong also praised his clarity and efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi served as recorder, and the prince also praised his clarity and efficiency.

sentences.zh: 及踐祚，即命維岳與畢士安權知開封府，拜給事中、知審官院。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he immediately appointed Weiyue together with Bi Shi'an to provisionally administer Kaifeng, conferred on Weiyue the title of Attendant Gentleman, and put him in charge of the Bureau for Review of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong took the throne he immediately appointed Weiyue and Bi Shi'an to provisionally administer Kaifeng, made Weiyue Attendant Gentleman, and put him in charge of the Bureau for Review of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 維岳體肥年衰，艱於拜趨，陳乞外遷小州。

translations.literal: Weiyue was corpulent and advanced in years, and found bowing and hurrying difficult; he petitioned to be transferred outward to a small prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue had grown stout and elderly and found court obeisance arduous; he asked to be transferred to a smaller prefecture in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其靜退，特授海州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor commended his quiet withdrawal and specially appointed him prefect of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his modest wish to withdraw and specially appointed him prefect of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，知蘇州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, he was made prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xianping era he was appointed prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 素病風，上以吳中多食魚蟹，乃徙壽州，仍命太醫馳療之。

translations.literal: He had long suffered from wind ailment; because Wu is rich in fish and crab, the emperor transferred him to Shou Prefecture and still ordered the imperial physicians to hurry to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: He had long suffered from a paralytic ailment. Because the lower Yangzi region abounds in fish and shellfish, the emperor transferred him to Shou Prefecture and sent imperial physicians to treat him.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 贈兵部侍郎，官給其葬。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Vice Minister of War, and his burial expenses were supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Minister of War, and the state provided for his burial.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，錄其孫世昌、獻之，並賜同學究出身。

translations.literal: During the Dazhong Xiangfu period, his grandsons Shichang and Xianzhi were entered on the register and both granted the status of fellow graduates of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong Xiangfu era his grandsons Shichang and Xianzhi were entered on the register and both granted the status of fellow graduates of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 維岳明習吏事，有治劇才。

translations.literal: Weiyue was well versed in administrative affairs and had talent for handling urgent business.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue was thoroughly versed in administrative affairs and had a gift for handling demanding duties.

sentences.zh: 在懷州，王欽若始舉進士，維岳知其貴；

translations.literal: While in Huai Prefecture, Wang Qinruo was just taking the jinshi examination; Weiyue knew he would rise high.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Huai Prefecture he met Wang Qinruo, who was then taking the jinshi examination, and recognized that he would rise high.

sentences.zh: 又善待陳彭年，自刺郡連奏為通判，皆稱薦之。

translations.literal: He also treated Chen Pengnian well; from the time he governed his own prefecture he repeatedly memorialized recommending him as vice commissioner, and in every case praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He also treated Chen Pengnian kindly. From the time he governed his own prefecture he repeatedly recommended Pengnian for vice commissioner, always speaking highly of him.

sentences.zh: 王陟

translations.literal: Wang Zhi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi

translations.literal: 〈Appended〉
translations.idiomatic: (Appended biography)

sentences.zh: 王陟者，潞州上黨人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi was a native of Shangdang in Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi came from Shangdang in Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年舉進士，補嵐州團練推官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed push officer of the Lianzhou Regiment.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 3 he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed push officer of the Lianzhou Regiment.

sentences.zh: 內侍羅懷嗣言其督運有勞，遷晉州觀察推官。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Luo Huaisi reported that his supervision of transport had been meritorious, and he was promoted to push officer of the Jin Prefecture Observation Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant Luo Huaisi reported his meritorious supervision of transport, and he was promoted to push officer of the Jin Observation Commission.

sentences.zh: 至道初，度支判官李擇言薦為著作佐郎、同判大名府，留知開封府司錄參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao, Revenue Commissioner Li Zeyan recommended him as Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation and Vice Commissioner of Daming Prefecture; he was retained as Recorder of the Kaifeng Prefecture Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Zhidao, Revenue Commissioner Li Zeyan recommended him as Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation and vice commissioner of Daming; he was retained as Recorder of the Kaifeng Prefecture Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 前司錄閻仲卿喜云為，屢升殿奏事，真宗尹京時頗不悅。

translations.literal: The former Recorder Yan Zhongqing was fond of boasting of his accomplishments and repeatedly ascended the hall to report affairs; when Zhenzong governed the capital as heir apparent he was quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The former Recorder Yan Zhongqing liked to boast of his accomplishments and repeatedly ascended the hall to report affairs; when Zhenzong governed the capital as heir apparent, he was quite displeased.

sentences.zh: 及陟代之，以謹幹聞，尤被待遇。

translations.literal: When Zhi replaced him, he became known for careful diligence and was especially favored.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi replaced him, he became known for careful diligence and was especially favored.

sentences.zh: 即位，召賜緋魚袋，改著作郎、開封府推官，乘傳陝西，與轉運使督饋靈武芻糧。

translations.literal: Upon accession he was summoned and granted the crimson fish bag; he was changed to Compiler and Push Officer of Kaifeng Prefecture, traveled by post relay to Shaanxi West, and with the transport commissioner supervised the delivery of forage to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Upon accession he was summoned and granted the crimson fish bag, made Compiler and Push Officer of Kaifeng, traveled by post relay to Shaanxi West, and with the transport commissioner supervised delivery of forage to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，遷太常博士，出為河東轉運使，賜金紫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, he was promoted to Doctor of the Grand Temple and went out as transport commissioner of Hedong, and was granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xianping era he was promoted to Doctor of the Grand Temple and posted as transport commissioner of Hedong, with the gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 時趙保吉納款，屢遣與內侍張崇貴裁度邊事，正其經界，又副崇貴使夏州賜誥命。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Baoji submitted his allegiance; he was repeatedly sent with the inner attendant Zhang Chonggui to settle border affairs and rectify the boundaries, and he also served as deputy to Chonggui when the latter was sent to Xia Prefecture to bestow patent letters.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Baoji submitted to the court, Zhi was repeatedly sent with the inner attendant Zhang Chonggui to settle border affairs and fix the boundaries. He also accompanied Chonggui to Xia Prefecture to deliver patent letters of appointment.

sentences.zh: 代歸，會溫仲舒知貢舉，命陟與刑部員外郎董龜正同考試及封印卷首。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, it happened that Wen Zhongshu was supervising the examinations; Zhi was ordered together with Vice Director of Punishments Dong Guizheng to examine candidates and seal the examination papers.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Wen Zhongshu was supervising the civil examinations, and Zhi was ordered together with Vice Director of Punishments Dong Guizheng to examine candidates and seal the papers.

sentences.zh: 俄改工部員外郎、知棣州。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Vice Director of Works and made prefect of Di Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Vice Director of Works and appointed prefect of Di Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五年，召歸，判三司鹽鐵勾院。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned back and made judge of the Salt and Iron Audit Office of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recalled and appointed judge of the Salt and Iron Audit Office of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 初，上以京府之舊，頗隆眷遇，將加擢用。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor, because of his old ties with the capital prefecture, had greatly favored him and was about to promote him further.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor, remembering his service in the capital prefecture, had favored him greatly and was about to promote him further.

sentences.zh: 會有言其在貢部，舉子有納賄成名者，恃恩寵，希顯要，僦大第以居，事遂寢。

translations.literal: It happened that someone reported that while in the examination bureau, candidates had gained success by bribery; relying on imperial favor, he coveted high office, and rented a large mansion to live in—the matter therefore lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Then word came that while supervising the examinations he had let candidates buy their success with bribes, that he relied on imperial favor to seek high office, and that he had rented a grand mansion to live in. The planned promotion was dropped.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died.

sentences.zh: 上甚憫之，錄其子若拙為奉禮郎，若谷為太廟齋郎。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly pitied him and entered his son Ruozhuo as Gentleman for Court Ceremony and Ruogu as Acolyte of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and entered his son Ruozhuo as Gentleman for Court Ceremony and Ruogu as Acolyte of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 後陟妻卒，又命給其子奉，使終喪制。

translations.literal: Later when Zhi's wife died, he again ordered stipends given to the sons so they could complete the mourning observances.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhi's wife died, he again ordered stipends for the sons so they could complete their mourning.

sentences.zh: 若拙官國子博士。

translations.literal: Ruozhuo held office as Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Ruozhuo later served as Erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 張雍，德州安德縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong, a native of Ande County in De Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong was a native of Ande County in De Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 治《毛氏詩》。

translations.literal: He studied the Mao Commentary on the Odes.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Mao Commentary on the Book of Odes.

sentences.zh: 開寶六年中第，釋褐東關尉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaibao he passed the examinations and on leaving office was made warden of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaibao he passed the examinations and on entering service was made warden of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，有薦其材者，召歸，改將作監丞、知南雄州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, someone recommended his talent; he was summoned back, changed to Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, and made prefect of Nanxiong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era someone recommended his ability. He was summoned to court, made Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, and appointed prefect of Nanxiong.

sentences.zh: 遷太子右贊善大夫、知開封府司錄參軍事，俄為秘書丞，充推官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Assistant in the Eastern Palace and made recorder of the Kaifeng prefectural government; soon he was made Secretary and served as investigating officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Assistant in the Eastern Palace and made recorder of Kaifeng, then soon became Secretary and served as investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 京城民王元吉者，母劉早寡，有奸狀，為姻族所知，憂悸成疾。

translations.literal: Among the capital's people was one Wang Yuanji; his mother Liu had been widowed early and had illicit relations, which the affinal kin knew; she became ill from anxiety and fear.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital there was a man named Wang Yuanji. His mother Liu had been widowed young and carried on an illicit affair that her kin knew about; tormented by fear and guilt, she fell ill.

sentences.zh: 又懼元吉告之，遂遣侍婢訴元吉寘堇食中以毒己，病將死。

translations.literal: She also feared Yuanji would report her, and therefore sent a serving maid to accuse Yuanji of putting poison in hellebore in her food to kill her; her illness was about to prove fatal.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Yuanji would expose her, she sent a maid to accuse him of poisoning her food with hellebore; she claimed she was near death.

sentences.zh: 事下右軍巡按之，未得實；

translations.literal: The case was sent to the Right Army Patrol for investigation, but the facts were not obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the Right Army Patrol, but no proof was found.

sentences.zh: 移左軍巡，推吏受劉賂掠治，元吉自誣伏。

translations.literal: It was transferred to the Left Army Patrol; the investigating clerks accepted Liu's bribe and tortured him until Yuanji confessed under duress.
translations.idiomatic: It was transferred to the Left Army Patrol. The investigators took bribes from Liu and tortured Yuanji until he confessed falsely.

sentences.zh: 俄而劉死，府慮囚，元吉始以實對。

translations.literal: Before long Liu died; fearing the prisoner, Yuanji then told the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liu died. Fearing for the prisoner, Yuanji at last told the truth.

sentences.zh: 又移付司錄，盡捕元推吏，稍見誣構之跡。

translations.literal: The case was again transferred to the recorder's office; all the original investigating clerks were arrested, and traces of the false construction gradually appeared.
translations.idiomatic: The case was sent again to the recorder's office. All the original investigators were arrested, and the frame-up gradually came to light.

sentences.zh: 且以逮捕者眾，又獄已累月未能決，府中懼其淹，列狀引見，詔免死決徒。

translations.literal: Moreover, because those arrested were numerous and the case had dragged on for months without resolution, the prefectural office feared delay; they submitted a memorial for audience and an edict commuted the death sentence to penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Because so many had been arrested and the case had dragged on for months, the prefectural office feared delay. They memorialized for an audience, and an edict commuted the death sentence to penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 元吉大呼曰：「府中官吏悉受我賂，反使我受刑乎？」

translations.literal: Yuanji cried out loudly: "All the officials of the prefecture took my bribes—are you now making me suffer punishment?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji cried out, "Every official in this prefecture took my bribes—will you now make me suffer punishment?"

sentences.zh: 府不敢決，元吉歷陳所受賂主名，又令妻張擊登聞鼓訴之。

translations.literal: The prefecture did not dare decide; Yuanji successively named those who had taken bribes from him, and also had his wife Zhang strike the petition drum before the palace gate to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture dared not decide the case. Yuanji named every official who had taken bribes from him, and his wife Zhang struck the petition drum at the palace gate to appeal.

sentences.zh: 上召張臨軒顧問，盡得其枉狀，立遣中使捕元推官吏，付御史鞫治。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Zhang before the throne to question her and fully learned the injustice; he immediately sent an inner attendant to arrest the original investigating clerks and deliver them to the censor for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zhang before the throne, learned the full injustice of the case, and immediately sent an inner attendant to arrest the original investigators and hand them to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 時滕中正為中丞，雍妻父也，詔供奉官蔚進別鞫之。

translations.literal: At that time Teng Zhongzheng was chief censor; Yong's wife's father—an edict ordered Palace Attendant Wei Jin to conduct a separate investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Zhongzheng was then chief censor and Yong's father-in-law, so an edict ordered Palace Attendant Wei Jin to conduct a separate investigation.

sentences.zh: 雍坐與知府劉保勳、判官李繼凝初慮問，元吉稱冤，徙左軍巡，雍戒吏止令鞫其毒母狀，致吏訊掠慘暴。

translations.literal: Yong was implicated because he and Prefect Liu Baoqin and Vice Magistrate Li Jining had at first feared questioning; when Yuanji claimed injustice the case was transferred to the Left Army Patrol. Yong instructed the clerks only to interrogate the charge of poisoning his mother, causing the investigators to torture with extreme cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was implicated because he and Prefect Liu Baoqin and Vice Magistrate Li Jining had at first feared the inquiry. When Yuanji protested his innocence the case went to the Left Army Patrol, and Yong told the clerks to investigate only the charge of poisoning his mother, which led to savage torture.

sentences.zh: 上怒，雍及左右軍巡判官韓昭裔、宋廷煦悉坐免所居官，保勳、繼凝各奪一等奉，左右軍巡使殿直龐則、王榮並降為殿前承旨。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; Yong and the investigating vice magistrates of the Left and Right Army Patrols Han Zhaoyi and Song Tingxu were all dismissed from their posts and forbidden to hold office; Baoqin and Jining each had one grade of salary taken away; the patrol commissioners of the Left and Right Army Patrols, Palace Direct Pang Ze and Wang Rong, were both demoted to Palace Attendants of the Front Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. Yong and the vice magistrates of the Left and Right Army Patrols, Han Zhaoyi and Song Tingxu, were all dismissed and forbidden to hold office. Baoqin and Jining each lost one grade of salary. The patrol commissioners Pang Ze and Wang Rong were demoted to attendants of the Front Hall.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，雍復為秘書丞、御史臺推直官，改鹽鐵推官，遷右補闕，充判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, Yong was again made Secretary, direct investigating officer of the Censorate, changed to Salt and Iron investigating officer, promoted to Right Remonstrator, and made judge.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yongxi era Yong was again made Secretary and direct investigating officer of the censorate, then Salt and Iron investigating officer, promoted to Right Remonstrator, and appointed judge.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，轉工部郎中、判度支勾院。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong, he was transferred to Director of Works and judge of the Revenue Audit Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Duangong era he was made Director of Works and judge of the Revenue Audit Office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又為鹽鐵判官兼判勾院。

translations.literal: Before long he again served as Salt and Iron judge concurrently judging the Audit Office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he again served as Salt and Iron judge while concurrently judging the Audit Office.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以本官兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: After more than a year, with his original rank he was concurrently Regular Attendant Censor supervising miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was made Regular Attendant Censor with supervisory duties, retaining his former rank.

sentences.zh: 月餘，出為淮南轉運使。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month he went out as transport commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later he was posted as transport commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，選為太府少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he was selected as Vice Director of the Grand Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Chunhua era he was selected as Vice Director of the Grand Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 二年，加右諫議大夫，徙兩浙轉運使，入知審刑院。

translations.literal: In the second year he was given the additional title of Right Remonstrating Grandee, transferred to transport commissioner of the two Zhe circuits, and entered to administer the Court for Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was given the additional title of Right Remonstrating Grandee, transferred to transport commissioner for the two Zhe circuits, and brought in to administer the Court for Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 三年，充戶部使，出知梓州，就命為西川轉運使，俄復知梓州。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made Revenue Commissioner, went out as prefect of Zizhou, was then appointed transport commissioner of Xichuan, and soon again made prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Revenue Commissioner, sent out as prefect of Zizhou, then appointed transport commissioner of Xichuan, and soon again made prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，蜀州青城民王小波、李順作亂，眾至萬人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Qingcheng commoners Wang Xiaobo and Li Shun rebelled; their forces reached ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Qingcheng commoners Wang Xiaobo and Li Shun rose in rebellion with a force of ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 雍訓練士卒，得城中兵三千餘人，又募強勇千餘守城，輦綿州金帛以實帑藏。

translations.literal: Yong trained soldiers and mustered more than three thousand troops in the city; he also recruited more than a thousand stalwart men to defend the walls and transported gold and silk from Mian Prefecture to fill the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Yong drilled the troops and mustered more than three thousand men in the city, recruited another thousand stalwart defenders, and brought gold and silk from Mian Prefecture to fill the treasury.

sentences.zh: 推官陳世卿治戎器，掌書記施謂、榷鹽院判官謝濤伐山木為竿，銷銅鍾為箭鏑，紐布為索，守械悉備。

translations.literal: Investigating Officer Chen Shiqing prepared weapons of war; Secretary Shi Wei and Salt Monopoly Vice Commissioner Xie Tao felled mountain timber for poles, melted bronze bells for arrowheads, twisted cloth into cords—the defensive equipment was all complete.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating officer Chen Shiqing prepared weapons. Secretary Shi Wei and salt monopoly vice commissioner Xie Tao felled mountain timber for poles, melted bronze bells for arrowheads, and twisted cloth into cords until every item of defense was ready.

sentences.zh: 遣推官盛梁請兵於朝。

translations.literal: He sent Investigating Officer Sheng Liang to request troops from court.
translations.idiomatic: He sent investigating officer Sheng Liang to request reinforcements from the court.

sentences.zh: 未幾，益綿邛彭漢州、永康軍悉陷於賊。

translations.literal: Before long, Yi, Mian, Qiong, Peng, Han prefectures and Yongkang Military District all fell to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yi, Mian, Qiong, Peng, Han, and Yongkang Military District all fell to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 順入成都，僭號大蜀王，勢甚盛，遣其黨楊廣將十萬眾寇劍門，相里貴帥眾十萬圍梓潼。

translations.literal: Shun entered Chengdu and arrogated the title King of Great Shu; his power was very strong. He sent his partisan Yang Guang with a hundred thousand men to attack Jianmen, and Xiangli Gui led a hundred thousand men to besiege Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Shun entered Chengdu and styled himself King of Great Shu. His power was formidable. He sent Yang Guang with a hundred thousand men against Jianmen and Xiangli Gui with a hundred thousand to besiege Zitong.

sentences.zh: 雍與監軍盧斌登堞望之，賊所出兵，皆老弱疲憊，無鎧甲，斌笑請開北門擊之，雍曰：「不可，賊或詐見老弱，設伏伺我。

translations.literal: Yong and Supervisor Lu Bin ascended the battlements to observe them; the troops the bandits sent out were all old, weak, and exhausted, without armor. Bin smiled and asked to open the north gate and strike them. Yong said: "That cannot be done. The bandits may be feigning weakness and setting an ambush to wait for us.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and army supervisor Lu Bin mounted the battlements to watch. The rebels' sortie troops were all old, weak, and unarmored. Bin smiled and asked to open the north gate and attack. Yong said, "No. They may be feigning weakness to lure us into an ambush.

sentences.zh: 又城中吏民心未定，脫為伏兵所突，則墮其奸計，非良策也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the officials and people in the city were not yet settled in mind; if we were suddenly rushed by ambush troops we would fall into their crafty scheme—this is not a good plan."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the officials and townspeople are still unsettled. If hidden troops rushed us, we would fall into their trap. That is no good strategy."

sentences.zh: 言未畢，果有卒依敵樓呼嘯，與外應和，雍亟斬以徇。

translations.literal: Before he had finished speaking, a soldier by the enemy tower indeed shouted in response to those outside; Yong immediately had him beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely finished when a soldier by the enemy tower shouted in answer to those outside. Yong had him beheaded at once as a warning.

sentences.zh: 賊大設梯衝火車，晝夜鼓噪，攻城益急，城中大恐，雍命發機石碎之，火箭雜下。

translations.literal: The bandits greatly set up scaling ladders, battering rams, and fire carts; day and night they beat drums and clamored, pressing the attack ever more urgently; great fear arose in the city. Yong ordered the catapults loosed to smash them, and fire arrows rained down in mixture.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels raised scaling ladders, battering rams, and fire carts, drumming and shouting day and night as the assault grew fiercer. Terror spread through the city. Yong ordered catapults to shatter their engines and mixed fire arrows to rain down.

sentences.zh: 賊稍退，復治攻具城西北隅，雍紿曰：「軍士趣治裝，吾將開東門擊賊。」

translations.literal: The bandits withdrew a little; they again prepared assault engines at the northwest corner of the wall. Yong deceived them, saying: "Soldiers, hurry to prepare your gear—I am going to open the east gate and strike the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels drew back slightly, then renewed their siege engines at the northwest corner. Yong deceived them, crying, "Men, make ready—I shall open the east gate and strike!"

sentences.zh: 陽遣步騎五百臨東門。

translations.literal: He openly sent five hundred infantry and cavalry to the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: He openly sent five hundred foot and horse soldiers to the east gate.

sentences.zh: 賊升牛頭山瞰城內，信然，伏精兵萬餘山之東隅以待我。

translations.literal: The bandits climbed Ox Head Mountain to look into the city and believed it; they hid more than ten thousand picked troops in the eastern foothills to wait for us.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels climbed Ox Head Mountain to peer into the city and believed him. They hid more than ten thousand picked troops on the mountain's eastern slope to await the sortie.

sentences.zh: 雍即召敢死士百輩縋而下，盡焚其攻具，自午達申殆盡，賊以為神。

translations.literal: Yong immediately summoned a hundred daredevils to be lowered by rope; they burned all the assault engines, and from noon until mid-afternoon they were nearly all destroyed; the bandits took it for divine intervention.
translations.idiomatic: Yong at once sent a hundred daredevils down by rope. They burned every siege engine; from noon until mid-afternoon nearly all were destroyed, and the rebels thought it supernatural.

sentences.zh: 凶黨數乘城進戰，皆不利。

translations.literal: The vicious partisans several times climbed the wall to join battle and were all unsuccessful.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chiefs stormed the walls several times and were repulsed each time.

sentences.zh: 一日，北風晝晦，賊乘風縱火，急攻北門。

translations.literal: One day the north wind blew and the day grew dark; the bandits took advantage of the wind to set fires and pressed the attack on the north gate.
translations.idiomatic: One day a north wind darkened the sky. The rebels used the wind to set fires and pressed hard on the north gate.

sentences.zh: 雍與盧斌等領兵據門，立矢石間，固守不動，賊為之少卻。

translations.literal: Yong together with Lu Bin and others led troops to hold the gate, standing amid arrows and stones, holding firm without moving; the bandits therefore slackened a little.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Lu Bin led troops to hold the gate, standing amid arrows and stones without yielding, until the rebels slackened their assault.

sentences.zh: 長圍八十餘日，會王繼恩遣石知顒來援，賊始潰去。

translations.literal: The long siege lasted more than eighty days; when Wang Jien sent Shi Zhiyong to bring relief, the bandits at last broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted more than eighty days. When Wang Jien sent Shi Zhiyong with relief troops, the rebels at last broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 遣施謂入奏，上手詔褒美，擢雍給事中，斌西京作坊使、領成州刺史，世卿掌書記，謂節度判官，濤觀察推官。

translations.literal: He sent Shi Wei to memorialize at court; the emperor personally wrote an edict of praise. Yong was promoted to Attendant Gentleman; Bin was made commissioner of the Western Capital workshops and given charge of Cheng Prefecture; Shiqing was made secretary; Shi Wei was made military commissioner's judge; Xie Tao was made investigating officer of the observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent Shi Wei to memorialize at court. The emperor wrote a personal edict of praise. Yong was promoted to Attendant Gentleman; Bin was made commissioner of the Western Capital workshops and given charge of Cheng Prefecture; Shiqing became secretary; Shi Wei military commissioner's judge; and Xie Tao investigating officer of the observation commission.

sentences.zh: 又以通判將作監丞趙賀為太子中舍，監軍供奉官辛規為內殿崇班。

translations.literal: He also made Vice Commissioner Zhao He of the Directorate of Palace Buildings Gentleman of the Palace Library, and Army Supervisor Palace Attendant Xin Gui Inner Palace Honored Companion.
translations.idiomatic: He also made vice commissioner Zhao He of the Directorate of Palace Buildings Gentleman of the Palace Library, and army supervisor palace attendant Xin Gui Inner Palace Honored Companion.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，改工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao he was changed to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao he was made Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 明年召歸，復知永興軍，轉禮部侍郎，改刑部，充度支使。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned back, again made administrator of Yongxing Military District, transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, changed to Punishments, and made Revenue Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled, again put in charge of Yongxing Military District, made Vice Minister of Rites, then Punishments, and appointed Revenue Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，遷鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping he was transferred to Salt and Iron Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianping he was made Salt and Iron Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上以雍齪齪小心，三司事重，宜有裁制，乃用王嗣宗代之。

translations.literal: The emperor considered Yong petty and cautious; the Three Departments' business was weighty and required decisive management, and therefore Wang Sizong was used to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Yong narrow and overcautious. The Three Departments' affairs were weighty and needed a firmer hand, so Wang Sizong was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 又以其無過，特拜戶部侍郎，復知審刑院，出知秦州，徙鳳翔府。

translations.literal: Moreover, because he had no fault, he was specially made Vice Minister of Revenue, again put in charge of the Court for Judicial Review, went out as prefect of Qin Prefecture, and was transferred to Fengxiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had committed no fault, he was specially made Vice Minister of Revenue, again put in charge of the Court for Judicial Review, sent out as prefect of Qin, and transferred to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 景德初，權知開封府事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he was given provisional charge of Kaifeng prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jingde era he was given provisional charge of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 上覽奏獄，京府囚二百餘人，以為淹繫，遣給事中董儼、直昭文館韓國華同慮問，決遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor reviewed memorials on prisons; the capital prefecture had more than two hundred prisoners, and he considered them long detained. He sent Attendant Gentleman Dong Yan and Direct Academician Han Guohua together to review the cases and decide their release.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing prison memorials, the emperor found more than two hundred detainees in the capital and considered them held too long. He sent Attendant Gentleman Dong Yan and Direct Academician Han Guohua to review the cases and release them.

sentences.zh: 三年，改兵部侍郎、同知審官院。

translations.literal: In the third year he was changed to Vice Minister of War and made concurrent administrator of the Bureau for Review of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Vice Minister of War and concurrent administrator of the Bureau for Review of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 明年，車駕朝陵，判留司尚書省，出知鄧州。

translations.literal: The next year, when the imperial carriage went to attend the imperial tombs, he was assigned to judge the capital ministry while the emperor was away, and then went out as prefect of Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the emperor went to the imperial tombs, Yong was left to judge the capital ministry in his absence, then sent out as prefect of Deng.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，請老，以尚書右丞致仕，誥命未至而卒，年七十。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu he requested retirement; he was granted retirement as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, but before the patent letter arrived he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu he asked to retire and was granted retirement as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, but died at seventy before the patent arrived.

sentences.zh: 雍性鄙吝，蒞事勤恪，善為米鹽苛察以肅下，恃其清幹，受遇於時，益矯厲以取名譽。

translations.literal: Yong was by nature mean and stingy; in office he was diligent and respectful, good at petty scrutiny of grain and salt to keep subordinates in order. Relying on his integrity and efficiency, he was favored in his time and became ever more severe to win reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was mean and stingy by nature. Diligent in office, he excelled at petty scrutiny of supplies to keep subordinates in line. Trusted for his integrity and efficiency, he grew ever harsher in pursuit of reputation.

sentences.zh: 所至藩鎮宴犒，率皆裁節；

translations.literal: Wherever he went, banquets and rewards for military commissioners were all cut back.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, banquets and rewards for military commissioners were sharply cut.

sentences.zh: 聚公錢為羨餘，以輸官帑；

translations.literal: He amassed public funds as surplus and delivered them to the government treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He amassed public funds as surplus and turned them in to the treasury.

sentences.zh: 集會賓佐，糲食而已。

translations.literal: When he gathered guests and aides, coarse food was all they had.
translations.idiomatic: When he entertained guests and aides, only coarse fare was served.

sentences.zh: 在三司置簿籍，有「按前急」、「馬前急」、「急中急」之目，頗為時論所誚。

translations.literal: In the Three Departments he set up ledgers with entries called "urgent by precedent," "urgent before the horse," and "urgent within urgent," which drew considerable ridicule from contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the Three Departments he kept ledgers with categories called "urgent by precedent," "urgent before the horse," and "urgent within urgent," which contemporaries mocked.

sentences.zh: 雍姿貌魯樸，始登科，為滕中正婿，中正子錫、世寧咸笑之。

translations.literal: Yong's appearance was rustic and plain. When he first passed the examinations he became the son-in-law of Teng Zhongzheng; Zhongzheng's sons Xi and Shining both laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong looked rustic and plain. When he first passed the examinations he married Teng Zhongzheng's daughter; Zhongzheng's sons Xi and Shining both laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 中正曰：「此人異日必顯達壽考，非汝曹所及。」

translations.literal: Zhongzheng said: "This man in time will certainly rise high and live long—this is not something you fellows can match."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzheng said, "This man will rise high and live long in the end—not something you can match."

sentences.zh: 錫兄弟雖有名，然終不越郎署，亦無耆年者。

translations.literal: Although the Xi brothers had reputation, in the end they never rose beyond the secretariat, nor did any reach old age.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi brothers won some fame, but neither rose beyond the secretariat nor lived to old age.

sentences.zh: 子太沖，官殿中丞。

translations.literal: His son Taichong held office as Vice Director in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Taichong served as Vice Director in the Palace.

sentences.zh: 董儼，字望之，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Dong Yan, courtesy name Wangzhi, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yan, whose courtesy name was Wangzhi, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年進士，解褐大理評事、通判饒州，加著作佐郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination; on leaving office he was made reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and vice commissioner of Rao Prefecture, and was given the additional title of Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination and entered service as reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and vice commissioner of Rao, with the additional title of Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation.

sentences.zh: 五年，授左拾遺、直史館。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Left Remembrancer and Direct Academician of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Left Remembrancer and Direct Academician of the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 轉右補闕，充淮南西路轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Remonstrator and made Vice Transport Commissioner of Huainan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Remonstrator and made Vice Transport Commissioner of Huainan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 會罷使，就命知光州。

translations.literal: When the commissionership was abolished, he was appointed on the spot prefect of Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the transport commission was abolished, he was appointed prefect of Guang on the spot.

sentences.zh: 儼狂躁務進，不樂外郡，上書乞還京師。

translations.literal: Yan was rash and restless in pursuit of advancement and disliked outer prefectures; he memorialized begging to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was rash and ambitious and disliked provincial posts; he memorialized asking to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒，降為秘書丞，削史館職，徙知忠州。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong was angry, demoted him to Secretary, stripped his historiography post, and transferred him to govern Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was angry, demoted him to Secretary, stripped his historiography post, and sent him to govern Zhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 復為右補闕，俄復直史館。

translations.literal: He was again made Right Remonstrator, and soon again Direct Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Right Remonstrator and soon restored as Direct Academician.

sentences.zh: 會併水陸發運為一，儼與王繼昇同領其事，就轉刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: When water and land transport were merged into one, Yan together with Wang Jisheng jointly led the affair and was transferred on the spot to Vice Director of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When water and land transport were merged, Yan and Wang Jisheng jointly headed the office, and he was made Vice Director of Punishments on the spot.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，進郎中、三司度支副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was promoted to Director and Vice Commissioner of Revenue in the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Duangong he was promoted to Director and Vice Commissioner of Revenue in the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 坐翟馬周事，左授海州團練副使，移知泰州。

translations.literal: He was implicated in the Zhai Mazhou affair, demoted on the left to Vice Commissioner of Military Training at Haizhou, and transferred to govern Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in the Zhai Mazhou affair, he was demoted to Vice Commissioner of Military Training at Haizhou and transferred to govern Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以戶部員外郎知泉州，召為京東轉運使。

translations.literal: After more than a year, as Vice Director of Revenue he was made prefect of Quanzhou, then summoned as transport commissioner of Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made Vice Director of Revenue and prefect of Quanzhou, then summoned as transport commissioner of Jingdong.

sentences.zh: 時三司改易制度，置三計使，因留拜右諫議大夫，充右計使。

translations.literal: At that time the Three Departments reformed their system and established three accounting commissioners; he was retained and made Right Remonstrating Grandee and Right Accounting Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Departments reformed their system and created three accounting commissioners, he was retained as Right Remonstrating Grandee and Right Accounting Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 使罷，出知揚州，遷右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When the commissionership was abolished he went out as prefect of Yangzhou and was transferred to Right Remonstrating Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When the post was abolished he went out as prefect of Yangzhou and was promoted to Right Remonstrating Grandee.

sentences.zh: 徙潭州，轉給事中，歷知廣、岳、洪三州、江陵府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Tan Prefecture, made Attendant Gentleman, and successively governed Guang, Yue, and Hong prefectures and Jiangling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Tan, made Attendant Gentleman, and successively governed Guang, Yue, and Hong prefectures and Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 景德中，歸朝。

translations.literal: During the Jingde period he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde era he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 會開封府繫囚二百餘人，朝議以其稽滯，命儼與韓國華、張雍同慮問，裁決之。

translations.literal: It happened that Kaifeng had more than two hundred prisoners under detention; court opinion held that the delay was excessive, and Yan was ordered together with Han Guohua and Zhang Yong to review the cases and decide them.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng then held more than two hundred prisoners. The court considered the delay excessive and ordered Yan, Han Guohua, and Zhang Yong to review and decide the cases.

sentences.zh: 俄判吏部銓，加工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was made judge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection board and given the additional title of Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made judge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection board and given the additional title of Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時黃觀罷西川轉運歸闕，儼與知雜御史王濟姻家，因託濟言於觀，求薦己知益州。

translations.literal: At that time Huang Guan, dismissed from transport commissioner of Xichuan, returned to court. Yan was related by marriage to Supervisory Censor Wang Ji and therefore asked Ji to speak to Guan on his behalf, seeking Guan's recommendation for himself as prefect of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Guan had just returned from dismissing his post as Xichuan transport commissioner. Yan was related by marriage to Supervisory Censor Wang Ji and asked Ji to speak to Guan, seeking recommendation as prefect of Yi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，觀復領陝西轉運，得對便殿，儼謂其必薦己。

translations.literal: Before long Guan again took charge of Shaanxi transport and was granted audience in the side hall; Yan supposed he would certainly recommend him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Guan again headed Shaanxi transport and was granted audience in the side hall; Yan assumed he would recommend him.

sentences.zh: 他日，面陳：「自以孤直不為權要所容，況黃觀庸淺無操持，恐為執政所使，妄有論薦，俾臣遠適，惟陛下察之。」

translations.literal: Another day he stated face to face: "I consider myself upright and isolated, not tolerated by the powerful. Moreover Huang Guan is shallow and without principle; I fear the chief ministers will use him to make reckless recommendations and send me far away—may Your Majesty investigate."
translations.idiomatic: Another day he said to the emperor's face, "I am upright and isolated, not tolerated by the powerful. Huang Guan is shallow and unprincipled; I fear the chief ministers will use him to recommend me for a distant post—may Your Majesty look into it."

sentences.zh: 真宗不之詰。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong did not question him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong did not press him.

sentences.zh: 數日，王濟得對，因述儼嘗有私託，且言：「儼性本矯詐，臣語觀不可許之。」

translations.literal: Several days later Wang Ji had audience and therefore related that Yan had once made a private request, and added: "Yan's nature is fundamentally deceitful; I told Guan he must not agree."
translations.idiomatic: Days later Wang Ji had audience and reported Yan's private request, adding, "Yan is fundamentally deceitful; I told Guan not to agree."

sentences.zh: 真宗不欲暴其事，乃出儼知青州。

translations.literal: Zhenzong did not wish to expose the matter, and therefore sent Yan out as prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong did not wish to expose the affair and sent Yan out as prefect of Qing.

sentences.zh: 儼復請對，言為權臣所擯，上慰遣之，久而不去，乃謂之曰：「爾自告黃觀求知益州，復有何人排斥乎？」

translations.literal: Yan again requested audience, saying he had been ostracized by powerful ministers. The emperor comforted and sent him off, but he lingered long without leaving; the emperor then said to him: "You yourself reported Huang Guan seeking appointment as prefect of Yi—who else is ostracizing you?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan again sought audience, claiming powerful ministers had ostracized him. The emperor comforted and dismissed him, but he lingered. The emperor said, "You yourself reported Huang Guan seeking Yi for you—who else is ostracizing you?"

sentences.zh: 儼即矍然，且言：「觀、濟嘗議益州須得臣往彈壓之。」

translations.literal: Yan was immediately startled and said: "Guan and Ji once discussed that Yi Prefecture required me to go and suppress it."
translations.idiomatic: Yan started and said, "Guan and Ji once said Yi required me to go and suppress troubles there."

sentences.zh: 上以其詞不類，因令條析以聞，復遣使陝西質問黃觀。

translations.literal: The emperor, because his words did not cohere, ordered him to set them out in detail and report, and again sent an envoy to Shaanxi to question Huang Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Because his account did not cohere, the emperor ordered a detailed memorial and sent an envoy to Shaanxi to question Guan.

sentences.zh: 觀具述儼託王濟求薦之事，且言儼素待臣非厚。

translations.literal: Guan fully related Yan's asking Wang Ji to seek recommendation, and added Yan had never treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Guan fully described Yan's request through Wang Ji and added that Yan had never treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 初，淳化中，儼為計使，觀為判官，儼知觀不飲酒，一日聚食，親酌以勸觀，觀為強飲之，有頃，都監趙贊召觀議事，觀即往，贊曰：「飲酒耶？」

translations.literal: Earlier, during Chunhua, Yan was accounting commissioner and Guan was vice commissioner. Yan knew Guan did not drink wine; one day at a gathering he personally poured wine to urge Guan, and Guan was forced to drink. Before long Director-General Zhao Zan summoned Guan to discuss business; Guan went at once. Zan said: "Have you been drinking?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in Chunhua, Yan was accounting commissioner and Guan his vice commissioner. Knowing Guan did not drink, Yan once pressed wine on him at a gathering until he drank against his will. Soon Director-General Zhao Zan summoned Guan on business. Zan asked, "Have you been drinking?"

sentences.zh: 觀以實對。

translations.literal: Guan answered truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Guan answered truthfully.

sentences.zh: 翌日，儼與贊密奏觀嗜酒廢職，故觀因是及之。

translations.literal: The next day Yan and Zan secretly memorialized that Guan was addicted to wine and neglected his duties; therefore Guan brought this up in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yan and Zan secretly memorialized that Guan drank to excess and neglected duty, which is why Guan raised it now.

sentences.zh: 乃詔樞密直學士劉綜與御史雜治之，儼方引伏，坐責授山南東道節度行軍司馬，不署州事。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Direct Academician of the Military Affairs Commission Liu Zong together with censors to investigate jointly; Yan had just confessed when he was punished and made marching administrator of Shannan East Circuit without charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Direct Academician Liu Zong and censors to investigate jointly. Yan had barely confessed when he was punished and made marching administrator of Shannan East Circuit without prefectural duties.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，會赦，起知郢州，病疽卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, when an amnesty was proclaimed, he was raised to govern Ying Prefecture; he died of carbuncle, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Dazhong Xiangfu an amnesty restored him to govern Ying, but he died of carbuncle at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 儼俊辯有材幹，不學無操行，所至厚納貨賂。

translations.literal: Yan was handsome in debate and had talent and efficiency, but did not study and had no moral conduct; wherever he went he heavily accepted bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was eloquent and capable but unlearned and without principle; wherever he went he took heavy bribes.

sentences.zh: 嘗令引贊吏改製朱衣，每夕納儼第，而潛以輕帛製衣易之。

translations.literal: Once he ordered the usher clerks to remake vermilion robes; each evening they brought them to Yan's residence while secretly exchanging them for light silk garments.
translations.idiomatic: Once he ordered usher clerks to remake vermilion robes; each evening they brought them to his house while secretly swapping them for lighter silk garments.

sentences.zh: 在銓司，命胥吏市物，及請其直，則嗬責之，其鄙屑如此。

translations.literal: In the selection bureau he ordered clerks to buy goods, and when they asked payment he berated them—he was petty to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: In the selection bureau he ordered clerks to buy goods, then berated them when they asked payment—petty to that degree.

sentences.zh: 又廣畜姬媵，頗事豪侈。

translations.literal: He also kept many concubines and was rather extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: He also kept many concubines and lived lavishly.

sentences.zh: 用傾狡圖位，終以是敗，士大夫醜之。

translations.literal: He used slander and cunning to seek position and in the end failed for it; scholar-officials despised him.
translations.idiomatic: He used slander and cunning to seek office and was ruined by it; scholar-officials despised him.

sentences.zh: 東封恩，復其官。

translations.literal: By the grace of the eastern feng he had his office restored.
translations.idiomatic: By the grace of the eastern feng rites his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 子仲容、仲宗，並為太子中舍。

translations.literal: His sons Zhongrong and Zhongzong were both made Gentlemen of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhongrong and Zhongzong were both made Gentlemen of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 兄偉至殿中丞致仕。

translations.literal: His elder brother Wei reached Vice Director in the Palace and retired.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Wei rose to Vice Director in the Palace and retired.

sentences.zh: 魏廷式

translations.literal: Wei Tingshi
translations.idiomatic: Wei Tingshi

sentences.zh: 魏廷式，字君憲，大名宗城人。

translations.literal: Wei Tingshi, courtesy name Junxian, was a native of Zongcheng in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Tingshi, whose courtesy name was Junxian, came from Zongcheng in Daming.

sentences.zh: 少明法學。

translations.literal: In youth he was well versed in legal studies.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was well versed in law.

sentences.zh: 嘗客遊趙州，舍於監軍魏咸美之廨，廨有西堂，素凶，咸美知廷式有膽氣，命居之，卒無恙。

translations.literal: Once while traveling as a guest in Zhao Prefecture he lodged in the office of Army Supervisor Wei Xianmei; the office had a west hall that was notoriously haunted. Xianmei knew Tingshi had courage and ordered him to live there; in the end nothing happened.
translations.idiomatic: Once while traveling in Zhao Prefecture he lodged in Army Supervisor Wei Xianmei's office, which had a west hall said to be haunted. Xianmei knew Tingshi was bold and had him stay there; nothing happened.

sentences.zh: 來京師，咸美弟咸信延置館舍，以同宗善待之。

translations.literal: Coming to the capital, Xianmei's younger brother Xianxin lodged him in a guest house and treated him kindly as a clansman.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, Xianmei's brother Xianxin lodged him in a guest house and treated him kindly as a kinsman.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年中第，釋褐朗州法曹掾。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the examinations; on leaving office he was made legal clerk of Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the examinations and entered service as legal clerk of Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 轉運使李惟清以其吏材奏，知桃源縣，遷將作監丞。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Li Weiqing memorialized his administrative talent; he was made prefect of Taoyuan County and transferred to Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Li Weiqing memorialized his administrative talent; he was made magistrate of Taoyuan and promoted to Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，改著作佐郎、通判潁州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was changed to Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation and made vice commissioner of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Duangong he was made Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation and vice commissioner of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，始命李昌齡判審刑院，以廷式明練刑章，奏為詳議官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, Li Changling was first appointed to judge the Court for Judicial Review; because Tingshi was well versed in penal statutes, he was memorialized as detailed deliberation officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua Li Changling was first appointed to judge the Court for Judicial Review; because Tingshi was expert in penal law, he was memorialized as detailed deliberation officer.

sentences.zh: 屢進對，太宗悅其明辨，遷太子左贊善大夫。

translations.literal: He repeatedly advanced for audience; Emperor Taizong was pleased with his clear discrimination and transferred him to Left Assistant in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly had audience; Taizong was pleased with his clarity and made him Left Assistant in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 時初較廷臣殿最，命廷式與樞密都承旨趙鎔、李著同勾當三班，多所規制。

translations.literal: At that time the court first compared the merits of capital officials; Tingshi was ordered together with Chief Protocol Officer of the Military Affairs Commission Zhao Rong and Li Zhu jointly to handle the third rank, and many regulations were established.
translations.idiomatic: When the court first ranked capital officials' merit, Tingshi was ordered with Chief Protocol Officer Zhao Rong and Li Zhu to handle the third rank and established many regulations.

sentences.zh: 越王生日，令持禮物賜之，超拜主客員外郎、判三司都勾院，換河南東道判官，改戶部員外郎、知利州。

translations.literal: On the Prince of Yue's birthday he was ordered to carry ritual gifts and bestow them; he was specially promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and made judge of the Three Departments Audit Office, exchanged to vice commissioner of Henan East Circuit, and changed to Vice Director of Revenue and prefect of Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the Prince of Yue's birthday he was sent with ritual gifts; he was specially promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and judge of the Three Departments Audit Office, exchanged to vice commissioner of Henan East Circuit, then made Vice Director of Revenue and prefect of Li.

sentences.zh: 李順為盜，就命充陝西至益州路轉運使。

translations.literal: When Li Shun became a bandit, he was appointed on the spot transport commissioner from Shaanxi West to Yizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shun rebelled he was appointed on the spot transport commissioner from Shaanxi West to Yizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 後入奏事，太宗謂曰：「有事當白中書。」

translations.literal: Later he entered to report affairs; Emperor Taizong said to him: "When there is business you should inform the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Later he entered to report; Taizong told him, "When there is business you should inform the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 廷式曰：「臣三千七百里外乘驛而至，以機事上聞，願取斷宸衷，非為宰相來也。」

translations.literal: Tingshi said: "Your subject came three thousand seven hundred li by post relay to report urgent affairs and wishes to obtain decision from the imperial mind—it is not for the chief minister that I have come."
translations.idiomatic: Tingshi said, "I have come three thousand seven hundred li by post to report urgent matters and seek the emperor's decision—not the chief minister's."

sentences.zh: 即不時召對，問方略稱旨，賜錢五十萬，令還任。

translations.literal: He was immediately summoned for unscheduled audience; his stratagems pleased the emperor, who bestowed five hundred thousand cash and ordered him to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned at once; his plans pleased the emperor, who gave him five hundred thousand cash and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 賊平，知寧州，未至，召入判大理寺。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified he was made prefect of Ning Prefecture; before he arrived he was summoned in to judge the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were pacified he was made prefect of Ning, but before arriving he was summoned to judge the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 至道初，乘傳河朔決獄，復出知宋、潭二州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao he traveled by post relay to Hebei to decide criminal cases; he then went out again as prefect of Song and Tan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhidao era he traveled by post relay through Hebei to decide criminal cases, then went out again as prefect of Song and Tan.

sentences.zh: 湖南地土衍沃，民喜訟產，有根柢巧偽難辨者，廷式立裁之，吏民咸服。

translations.literal: Hunan's land was broad and fertile; the people were fond of litigating over property, and where there were deep roots of cunning forgery hard to distinguish, Tingshi settled them on the spot, and officials and commoners alike submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan was broad and fertile, and the people were prone to property lawsuits with tangled roots of cunning forgery that were hard to tell apart; Tingshi settled such cases on the spot, and officials and commoners alike submitted.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部員外郎、知桂州，歷工部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and made prefect of Gui Prefecture, and served as Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and appointed prefect of Gui, then served as Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，改刑部。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong acceded, he was changed to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded he was moved to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 會王繼恩有罪下吏，命廷式同按之，逾宿而獄具。

translations.literal: When Wang Jien was found guilty and handed over to officials, Tingshi was ordered jointly to investigate; within a night the case was complete.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jien was found guilty and handed to the authorities, Tingshi was ordered to investigate jointly with others; within a night the case was complete.

sentences.zh: 俄知審官院、通進銀臺封駁司，拜右諫議大夫、知審刑院，出知涇州。

translations.literal: Soon he was made director of the Bureau for Reviewing Appointments and of the Office for Forwarding Memorials and Sealed Rebuttals; he was appointed Right Remonstrance and Reviewing Officer and director of the Court for Judicial Punishments, then went out as prefect of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he directed the Bureau for Reviewing Appointments and the Office for Forwarding Memorials and Sealed Rebuttals, was appointed Right Remonstrance and Reviewing Officer and director of the Court for Judicial Punishments, and then went out as prefect of Jing.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 2 he died, aged forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 錄其子攝太常寺太祝舜卿為太祝，禹卿同學究出身。

translations.literal: His son Shunqing, who was acting Master of Ceremonies of the Grand Temple, was entered on the register as Master of Ceremonies; Yuging likewise received the status of fellow graduate of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shunqing, then acting Master of Ceremonies of the Grand Temple, was entered on the register as Master of Ceremonies, and Yuging likewise received the status of fellow graduate of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 廷式所至，以嚴明稱，剛果敢言，為人主厚遇，然性傾險，喜中傷人，士君子憚其口而鄙其行。

translations.literal: Wherever Tingshi went he was known for severity and clarity; he was resolute and dared to speak, and was greatly favored by the ruler—but his nature was treacherous and he delighted in slandering others; scholar-gentlemen feared his mouth and despised his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Tingshi went he was known for severity; resolute and outspoken, he won the ruler's favor—but he was treacherous and delighted in slander, and gentlemen feared his tongue and despised his ways.

sentences.zh: 盧琰，字錫珪，淄州淄川人。

translations.literal: Lu Yan, courtesy name Xigui, was a native of Zichuan in Zi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yan, whose courtesy name was Xigui, came from Zichuan in Zi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父浚，右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: His father Jun was Right Remonstrating Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun was Right Remonstrating Grandee.

sentences.zh: 琰太平興國八年進士舉，解褐歷城主簿。

translations.literal: Yan passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo; on leaving office he was made registrar of Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan passed the jinshi in the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo and entered service as registrar of Licheng.

sentences.zh: 歷大理評事、知安吉縣。

translations.literal: He served as reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and governed Anji County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and governed Anji County.

sentences.zh: 三遷太常丞、通判幷州。

translations.literal: After three promotions he was Vice Director of the Grand Temple and vice commissioner of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he was Vice Director of the Grand Temple and vice commissioner of Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至道中，就加太常博士。

translations.literal: During the Zhidao period he was given on the spot the additional title of Doctor of the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhidao he was given on the spot the additional title of Doctor of the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，選為開封府判官，與推官李防並命。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he was selected as judge of Kaifeng and appointed together with investigating officer Li Fang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping he was selected as judge of Kaifeng together with investigating officer Li Fang.

sentences.zh: 真宗謂宰相曰：「人之有材，難得盡知，但歷試而後可見。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong told the chief ministers: "A man's talent is hard to know fully; only after repeated trials can it be seen."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong told the chief ministers, "Talent is hard to know fully; only repeated trials reveal it."

sentences.zh: 占謝日，特升殿，諭以天府事繁慎選之意，仍賜緡錢。

translations.literal: On the day of his audience of thanks he was specially advanced to the hall; he was instructed on the meaning of the careful selection because the capital prefecture's business was complex, and was still granted silk cash.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he thanked the throne he was specially received in the hall, told why the capital post demanded careful selection, and granted silk cash.

sentences.zh: 會獄空，有詔獎之。

translations.literal: When the prisons were empty an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When the prisons stood empty an edict praised him.

sentences.zh: 遷工部員外郎，為河北轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of Works and made Vice Transport Commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of Works and Vice Transport Commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 時北鄙未寧，調發軍儲，糧道不絕。

translations.literal: At that time the northern border was not yet settled; military stores were mobilized without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The northern border was not yet settled and military supplies moved without cease.

sentences.zh: 以職務修舉，召入，遷秩刑部，賜金紫，復遣之任。

translations.literal: Because his duties were well performed he was summoned, promoted in the Ministry of Punishments, granted gold and purple, and again sent to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Because his duties were well performed he was summoned, promoted in the Ministry of Punishments, granted gold and purple, and sent back.

sentences.zh: 會城祁州，命專董其役。

translations.literal: When Qi Prefecture was being walled he was ordered to supervise the work exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Prefecture was being walled he was ordered to supervise the work.

sentences.zh: 契丹入邊，車駕幸澶州，琰自定州隨軍至大名，即單騎赴行在。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded the border the imperial carriage went to Chanyuan; Yan followed the army from Ding Prefecture to Daming, then rode alone to the temporary palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded, the emperor went to Chanyuan. Yan followed from Ding to Daming, then rode alone to the temporary palace.

sentences.zh: 召對，勞問久之。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, the emperor questioned and comforted him at length.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for audience, the emperor questioned and comforted him at length.

sentences.zh: 其子士宗時為隰州推官，特遷大理寺丞。

translations.literal: His son Shizong was then investigating officer of Xi Prefecture and was specially transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shizong was then investigating officer of Xi Prefecture and was specially made Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 契丹請和，琰上言領職六年，求歸闕，許之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan sought peace Yan memorialized that he had held his post six years and begged to return to court; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan sought peace Yan memorialized that he had served six years and begged to return; this was granted.

sentences.zh: 以使勞，優拜吏部員外郎、判三司三勾院。

translations.literal: Because of his commissioner's labors he was favorably promoted to Vice Director of Personnel and judge of the Three Departments' three audit offices.
translations.idiomatic: For his service as commissioner he was favorably made Vice Director of Personnel and judge of the Three Departments' three audit offices.

sentences.zh: 會宋摶使契丹，命權戶部副使。

translations.literal: When Song Tuan was envoy to the Khitan he was ordered provisionally Vice Commissioner of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Tuan went as envoy to the Khitan he was made provisional Vice Commissioner of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時議東封，又權京東轉運使，往營頓置。
