translations.literal: When the eastern feng was discussed he was again provisionally made transport commissioner of Jingdong to go arrange encampments.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern feng was discussed he was again made provisional transport commissioner of Jingdong to arrange encampments.

sentences.zh: 加戶部郎中，復判三勾院。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Director in the Ministry of Revenue and again made judge of the three audit offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director in the Ministry of Revenue and again judge of the three audit offices.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，以本官兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, with his original rank he was concurrently Regular Attendant Censor supervising miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was made Regular Attendant Censor with supervisory duties, retaining his rank.

sentences.zh: 數月，授三司度支副使。

translations.literal: After several months he was appointed Vice Commissioner of Revenue in the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was appointed Vice Commissioner of Revenue in the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰歲，命與鮑中和同判留守司三司，加吏部郎中，俄拜右諫議大夫、知永興軍府。

translations.literal: In the year of the feng sacrifice at Fenyin he was ordered together with Bao Zhonghe jointly to judge the capital ministry's Three Departments while the emperor was away; he was given the additional title of Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and soon made Right Remonstrating Grandee and administrator of Yongxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the year of the Fenyin feng he and Bao Zhonghe were ordered to judge the capital ministry's Three Departments during the emperor's absence; he was made Director in Personnel, then Right Remonstrating Grandee and administrator of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 五年，再為河北轉運使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again became transport commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again became transport commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 琰勤於吏職，所至以幹集聞。

translations.literal: Yan was diligent in administrative duties; wherever he went he was known for capable accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was diligent in office; wherever he served he was known for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 頗知命，嘗語親舊曰：「官五品，服三品，天不與者壽爾。」

translations.literal: He was rather versed in fate and once told relatives and friends: "At the fifth rank of office, wearing third-rank robes—if Heaven does not grant it, there will be no long life."
translations.idiomatic: He believed in fate and once told kin, "Fifth-rank office in third-rank robes—if Heaven does not grant it, life will not be long."

sentences.zh: 明年被疾，詔遣中使將太醫診視。

translations.literal: The next year he fell ill; an edict sent an inner attendant with imperial physicians to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he fell ill; an edict sent an inner attendant with imperial physicians to treat him.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 時琰母八十餘，無恙，上憫之，以士宗為太常博士，特命知懷州；

translations.literal: At that time Yan's mother was more than eighty and in good health; the emperor pitied her, made Shizong Erudite of the Grand Temple, and specially appointed him prefect of Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's mother was over eighty and still healthy; the emperor pitied her, made Shizong Erudite of the Grand Temple, and specially appointed him prefect of Huai.

sentences.zh: 又以次子秘書丞士倫為太常博士，給祿終喪。

translations.literal: His second son, Secretary Cheng Shilun, was also made Erudite of the Grand Temple and given stipends through the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Secretary Shilun was also made Erudite of the Grand Temple with stipends through mourning.

sentences.zh: 士倫至工部郎中、度支副使，士宗自有傳。

translations.literal: Shilun reached Director of Works and Vice Commissioner of Revenue; Shizong has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shilun rose to Director of Works and Vice Commissioner of Revenue; Shizong has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 宋摶，字鵬舉，萊州掖人。

translations.literal: Song Tuan, courtesy name Pengju, was a native of Ye in Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song Tuan, whose courtesy name was Pengju, came from Ye in Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 治《毛氏詩》。

translations.literal: He studied the Mao Commentary on the Odes.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Mao Commentary on the Book of Odes.

sentences.zh: 開寶八年，宋準典貢部，得第，調補遂寧尉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaibao, Song Zhun supervised the examinations; Tuan passed and was appointed supplementing Suining warden.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kaibao, when Song Zhun supervised the examinations, Tuan passed and was appointed warden of Suining.

sentences.zh: 歷濰州司理參軍，改白龍令。

translations.literal: He served as judicial administrator of Wei Prefecture and was changed to magistrate of Bailong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial administrator of Wei Prefecture, then became magistrate of Bailong.

sentences.zh: 膳部員外郎鞠礪薦其能，遷右贊善大夫、知利豐監，徙知藤州。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Ministry of Provisions Ju Li recommended his ability; he was transferred to Right Assistant in the Eastern Palace and made administrator of Lifeng Directorate, then transferred to govern Teng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Li of the Ministry of Provisions recommended him; he was made Right Assistant in the Eastern Palace and administrator of Lifeng Directorate, then transferred to Teng.

sentences.zh: 改殿中丞、通判洪州。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director in the Palace and made vice commissioner of Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director in the Palace and vice commissioner of Hong.

sentences.zh: 復有薦者，召還，命提點河北西路刑獄，未行，改監左藏庫。

translations.literal: Again someone recommended him; he was summoned back and ordered to supervise penal affairs on Hebei West Circuit, but before departing was changed to supervise the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended again, he was recalled to supervise penal affairs on Hebei West Circuit, but before leaving was made supervisor of the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 遷國子博士、通判西京留守司，得對便坐，賜錢三十萬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the Directorate of Education and vice commissioner of the Western Capital garrison headquarters; he was granted audience in the side seat and given three hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Erudite of the Directorate of Education and vice commissioner of the Western Capital garrison, granted audience in the side seat, and given three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 久之，徙江南轉運使，就遷度支員外郎。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to transport commissioner of Jiangnan and promoted on the spot to Vice Director of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was made transport commissioner of Jiangnan and promoted on the spot to Vice Director of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 真宗嗣位，遷司封員外郎、河東轉運使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong succeeded, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Provisions and made transport commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong succeeded he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Provisions and transport commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 上言：「大通監冶鐵盈積，可備諸州軍數十年鼓鑄，願權罷採以紓民。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The Datong Directorate's iron smelting has accumulated in surplus and could supply the military prefectures' casting needs for several decades; I beg permission temporarily to halt collection to relieve the people."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Datong Directorate iron has piled up enough to supply prefectural casting for decades; I beg a temporary halt in collection to relieve the people."

sentences.zh: 又請科諸州丁壯為兵，以增戎備。

translations.literal: He also requested levying able-bodied men from the prefectures as soldiers to increase military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to levy able-bodied men from the prefectures as soldiers to strengthen defenses.

sentences.zh: 在任凡十一年。

translations.literal: In office altogether eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post eleven years in all.

sentences.zh: 河東接西北境，時邊事未息，屯師甚廣，摶經制漕運，以幹治稱。

translations.literal: Hedong bordered the northwest frontier; border affairs had not yet ceased and stationed troops were very numerous; Tuan managed transport and was known for capable administration.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong bordered the northwest; troops remained massed on the frontier, and Tuan managed transport with a reputation for efficiency.

sentences.zh: 連他徙，州郡輒乞留，有詔褒飭。

translations.literal: Whenever he was transferred elsewhere, prefectures and districts begged to keep him; an edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever transfer was proposed, prefectures begged to keep him; an edict commended his service.

sentences.zh: 兩至夏州界部發居民，數詣闕奏事稱旨。

translations.literal: Twice he went to the Xia Prefecture border to deploy residents and several times memorialized at court to the emperor's satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he went to the Xia border to deploy residents and several times memorialized at court to the emperor's satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 屢以秩滿請代，朝議以摶善職，就加祠部郎中，賜金紫。

translations.literal: Repeatedly when his term expired he requested replacement; court opinion held that Tuan excelled in his post, and he was given on the spot the additional title of Director in the Ministry of Rites and granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he repeatedly asked to be replaced, but the court valued his service and gave him on the spot the additional title of Director in the Ministry of Rites with gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 嘗薦代州承受使臣王白，上以本置此職，止於視軍政、察邊事，摶不應保奏。

translations.literal: Once he recommended Dai Prefecture reception commissioner Wang Bai; the emperor said this post was originally established only to observe military government and inspect border affairs—Tuan should not have recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he recommended Dai reception commissioner Wang Bai; the emperor said that post was only to observe military affairs and inspect the border—Tuan should not have recommended him.

sentences.zh: 因詔諸路，自今勿得舉承受使臣。

translations.literal: An edict therefore ordered all circuits that from now on they must not recommend reception commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered all circuits never again to recommend reception commissioners.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，入判三司勾院，逾月，為戶部副使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde he entered as judge of the Three Departments Audit Office; after more than a month he was made Vice Commissioner of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jingde he became judge of the Three Departments Audit Office; a month later he was made Vice Commissioner of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，進秩刑部郎中，俄使契丹，會疾，契丹主以車迎之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he was promoted in rank to Director in the Ministry of Punishments; soon he was envoy to the Khitan, and when he fell ill the Khitan ruler sent a carriage to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Dazhong Xiangfu he was promoted to Director in Punishments; soon sent as envoy to the Khitan, when he fell ill the Khitan ruler sent a carriage to meet him.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 子可法至太子中舍，舜元登進士第。

translations.literal: His son Kefa reached Gentleman of the Palace Library; Shunyuan passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kefa rose to Gentleman of the Palace Library; Shunyuan passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 摶卒，舜元自筠州判官改著作佐郎。

translations.literal: When Tuan died, Shunyuan was changed from judge of Yun Prefecture to Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuan died, Shunyuan was changed from judge of Yun to Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation.

sentences.zh: 又賜其孫出身。

translations.literal: His grandson was also granted graduate status.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson was also granted graduate status.

sentences.zh: 凌策，字子奇，宣州涇人。

translations.literal: Ling Ce, courtesy name Ziqi, was a native of Jing in Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Ce, whose courtesy name was Ziqi, came from Jing in Xuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世給事州縣。

translations.literal: For generations the family served in prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family served in prefectural and district offices.

sentences.zh: 策幼孤，獨厲志好學，宗族初不加禮，因決意渡江，與姚鉉同學於廬州。

translations.literal: Ce was orphaned young, alone cultivated his will and loved learning; at first his clan did not treat him with courtesy, and therefore he resolved to cross the Yangzi and study at Luzhou together with Yao Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Ce studied diligently though his clan at first showed him no courtesy; he crossed the Yangzi to study at Luzhou with Yao Xian.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年舉進士，起家廣安軍判官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he passed the jinshi examination and began his career as judge of Guangan Military District.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he passed the jinshi and began as judge of Guangan Military District.

sentences.zh: 改西川節度推官，以強幹聞。

translations.literal: He was changed to investigating officer of the Xichuan military commission and became known for forceful capability.
translations.idiomatic: He became investigating officer of the Xichuan military commission and was known for forceful capability.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，就命為光祿寺丞，簽書兩使判官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua he was appointed on the spot Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and signing secretary for the two commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunhua he was made on the spot Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and signing secretary for the two commissioners.

sentences.zh: 代還，拜左贊善大夫、通判定州，賜朱衣、銀章、御書曆，給以實奉。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned he was made Left Assistant in the Eastern Palace and vice commissioner of Ding Prefecture; he was granted vermilion robes, silver seal, and an imperial calendar, and given full salary.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Left Assistant in the Eastern Palace and vice commissioner of Ding, granted vermilion robes, silver seal, and an imperial calendar with full salary.

sentences.zh: 李順之亂，川陝選官多憚行，策自陳三蒞蜀境，諳其民俗，即命知蜀州。

translations.literal: When Li Shun rebelled, many officials selected for Chuan and Shaanxi feared to go; Ce volunteered that he had thrice served in Shu territory and knew its customs, and was immediately appointed prefect of Shu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shun rebelled, many officials feared posting to Sichuan and Shaanxi. Ce volunteered that he had served three times in Shu and knew its customs, and was immediately made prefect of Shu.

sentences.zh: 又以巴西當益之餫道，徙綿州，加太常博士。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Baxi was on Yi's supply route, he was transferred to Mian Prefecture and given the additional title of Doctor of the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Because Baxi lay on Yi's supply route, he was transferred to Mian and given the additional title of Doctor of the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 還朝，會命為廣南西路轉運使，進屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was appointed transport commissioner of Guangnan West Circuit and promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue for state farms.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was made transport commissioner of Guangnan West Circuit and promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue for state farms.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部判官，遷都官。

translations.literal: He entered as judge of the Ministry of Revenue and was transferred to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as judge of the Ministry of Revenue and was transferred to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 先是，嶺南輸香藥，以郵置卒萬人，分鋪二百，負擔抵京師，且以煩役為患。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lingnan submitted aromatics and medicines; ten thousand postal runners in two hundred stations carried loads to the capital, and this was also considered a troublesome corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lingnan sent aromatics by post, with ten thousand runners at two hundred stations bearing loads to the capital—a burdensome corvée.

sentences.zh: 詔策規制之，策請陸運至南安，泛舟而北，止役卒八百，大省轉送之費。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ce to plan the system; Ce requested transport by land to Nan'an, then shipment by boat north, limiting the corvée to eight hundred men and greatly reducing transfer costs.
translations.idiomatic: Ce was ordered to reform the system. He proposed land transport to Nan'an, then shipment north by boat, cutting the corvée to eight hundred men and greatly reducing costs.

sentences.zh: 盧之翰任廣州，無廉稱，以策有幹名，拜職方員外郎、直史館，命代之，賜金紫。

translations.literal: Lu Zhihan governed Guangzhou without reputation for integrity; because Ce had a name for capability, he was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and Direct Academician and ordered to replace him, and was granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhihan governed Guangzhou without integrity; because Ce was known for capability, he was made Vice Director in Works and Direct Academician to replace him, with gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 廣、英路自吉河趣板步二百里，當盛夏時瘴起，行旅死者十八九。

translations.literal: The Guang and Ying route from Ji River toward Banbu for two hundred li, when midsummer miasma rose, killed eight or nine of ten travelers.
translations.idiomatic: On the Guang and Ying route from Ji River to Banbu, two hundred li through midsummer miasma killed eight travelers in ten.

sentences.zh: 策請由英州大源洞伐山開道，直抵曲江，人以為便。

translations.literal: Ce requested a route through Dayuan Cave in Ying Prefecture, felling mountains to open a road straight to Qujiang; people considered it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Ce proposed a route through Dayuan Cave in Ying, cutting a road straight to Qujiang; travelers found it far easier.

sentences.zh: 代還，知青州。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned he was made prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made prefect of Qing.

sentences.zh: 東封，以供億之勤，超拜都官郎中，入判三司三勾院，出知揚州。

translations.literal: For the eastern feng, because of his diligence in provisioning, he was specially promoted to Director in the Ministry of Justice, entered as judge of the Three Departments' three audit offices, and went out as prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For the eastern feng his provisioning won special promotion to Director in Justice; he judged the three audit offices, then went out as prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬江、淮歲儉，頗有盜賊，以策領淮南東路安撫使。

translations.literal: It happened that the Jiang and Huai region had a lean year and there were rather many bandits; Ce was made pacification commissioner of Huainan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang and Huai region then suffered famine and banditry; Ce was made pacification commissioner of Huainan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 駕旋，使停，進秩司封。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned the commission was halted; he was promoted in the Ministry of Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned the pacification commission ended and he was promoted in the Ministry of Provisions.

sentences.zh: 時洪州水，知州李玄病，上與宰相歷選朝士，將徙策代之。

translations.literal: At that time Hong Prefecture suffered flood; Prefect Li Xuan was ill; the emperor with the chief ministers successively selected capital officials and was about to transfer Ce to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Prefecture then suffered flood and Prefect Li Xuan was ill; the emperor and chief ministers were about to transfer Ce to replace him.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「南昌水潦艱殆，長吏當便宜從事，不必稟於外計也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Nanchang in flood is perilous; the chief administrator should act as circumstances require and need not report to the outer transport commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Nanchang in flood is dire; its chief must act as circumstances require without waiting on the transport commissioner."

sentences.zh: 王旦言：「策蒞事和平，可寄方面，望即以江南轉運使授之，仍詔諭差選之意。」

translations.literal: Wang Dan said: "Ce handles affairs peacefully and can be entrusted with a circuit; I hope he may be given Jiangnan transport commissioner at once, with an edict explaining the special selection."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan said, "Ce is steady in office and can govern a circuit; give him Jiangnan transport at once, with an edict explaining the special choice."

sentences.zh: 饒州產金，嘗禁商市鬻，或有論告，逮繫滿獄。

translations.literal: Raozhou produced gold; trade had been forbidden, and when there were accusations people were arrested until the prisons were full.
translations.idiomatic: Raozhou produced gold; trade had been forbidden, and accusations filled the prisons.

sentences.zh: 策請縱民販市，官責其算，人甚便之。

translations.literal: Ce requested that the people be allowed to sell in the market while the government collected duty; people found it very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Ce asked that trade be allowed with official duty collected; the people found it greatly convenient.

sentences.zh: 五年，召拜右諫議大夫、集賢殿學士、知益州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned and made Right Remonstrating Grandee, Academician of the Hall for Treasuring Literature, and prefect of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was summoned as Right Remonstrating Grandee, Academician of the Hall for Treasuring Literature, and prefect of Yi.

sentences.zh: 初，策登第，夢人以六印加劍上遺之，其後往劍外凡六任，時以為異。

translations.literal: When Ce first passed the examinations he dreamed that a man gave him six seals added to a sword; afterward he went to the sword regions six times in all, and the time considered it strange.
translations.idiomatic: When Ce passed the examinations he dreamed a man gave him six seals on a sword; he later served six times in the sword regions, which people thought strange.

sentences.zh: 策勤吏職，處事精審，所至有治跡。

translations.literal: Ce was diligent in office, handled affairs with precision, and wherever he went left traces of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Ce was diligent and precise in office and wherever he served left a record of good governance.

sentences.zh: 九年，自蜀代還，上頗有意擢用，會已病，命知通進銀臺司兼門下封駁事，糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he returned from Shu; the emperor was quite minded to promote him, but he was already ill and was ordered to administer the Directorate for Advancement of Silver Platforms concurrently with gate review and rebuttal, investigating capital penal cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he returned from Shu; the emperor wished to promote him, but he was already ill and was ordered to administer the Directorate for Advancement of Silver Platforms with gate review and capital penal investigation.

sentences.zh: 真宗嘗對王旦言：「策有才用，治蜀敏而有斷。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong once said to Wang Dan: "Ce has talent and ability; in governing Shu he is sharp and decisive."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong once told Wang Dan, "Ce is talented; in governing Shu he is sharp and decisive."

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「策性淳質和，臨事強濟。」

translations.literal: Dan said: "Ce's nature is honest, plain, and harmonious; in affairs he is forceful and effective."
translations.idiomatic: Dan said, "Ce is honest and harmonious by nature, but forceful and effective in affairs."

sentences.zh: 上深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply agreed.

sentences.zh: 是秋，拜給事中、權御史中丞。

translations.literal: That autumn he was made Attendant Gentleman and provisional Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was made Attendant Gentleman and provisional Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時榷茶之法弊甚，詔與翰林學士李迪、知雜御史呂夷簡同議經制，稍寬其舊。

translations.literal: At that time the monopoly tea law was greatly defective; an edict ordered him together with Hanlin Academician Li Di and Supervisory Censor Lü Yijian jointly to deliberate regulations, and the old law was somewhat relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: The tea monopoly law was then greatly defective; he was ordered with Hanlin Academician Li Di and Supervisory Censor Lü Yijian to revise it, and the old rules were somewhat relaxed.

sentences.zh: 明年，疾甚，不能朝謁，累遣中使挾醫存問，賜名藥。

translations.literal: The next year his illness was severe and he could not attend court; the emperor repeatedly sent inner attendants with physicians to inquire and bestowed famous medicines.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was too ill for court; the emperor repeatedly sent physicians with famous medicines.

sentences.zh: 復表求典益，尋遷工部侍郎，從其請。

translations.literal: He again memorialized begging to administer Yi; soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He again begged to govern Yi; soon he was made Vice Minister of Works and his request granted.

sentences.zh: 天禧二年三月卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Tianxi he died, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Tianxi he died at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 錄其子將作監主簿瓘、琬並為奉禮郎，續給其奉。

translations.literal: His sons Guan and Wan, chief clerks of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, were both made Gentlemen for Court Ceremony, and stipends were continued.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Guan and Wan, clerks of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, were both made Gentlemen for Court Ceremony with continued stipends.

sentences.zh: 策兄簡，官國子博士，分司南京。

translations.literal: Ce's elder brother Jian was Erudite of the Directorate of Education, assigned to the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ce's elder brother Jian was Erudite of the Directorate of Education at the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 楊覃，字申錫，漢太尉震之後。

translations.literal: Yang Tan, courtesy name Shenxi, was a descendant of the Han Grand Commandant Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tan, whose courtesy name was Shenxi, was a descendant of the Han Grand Commandant Yang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 唐有京兆尹憑居履道坊，僕射於陵居新昌坊，刑部尚書汝士居靖恭坊，時稱「三楊」，皆為盛門，而靖恭尤著。

translations.literal: In Tang there was Metropolitan Governor Ping dwelling in Lüdao Ward, Vice Director Yuling in Xinchang Ward, and Minister of Punishments Rushi in Jinggong Ward; the time called them the "Three Yangs," all eminent houses, but Jinggong was especially renowned.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang, Metropolitan Governor Ping lived in Lüdao Ward, Vice Director Yuling in Xinchang, and Minister of Punishments Rushi in Jinggong—the "Three Yangs," all great houses, Jinggong especially renowned.

sentences.zh: 汝士弟虞卿、漢公、魯士皆顯名。

translations.literal: Rushi's younger brothers Yuqing, Hangong, and Lushi were all illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: Rushi's younger brothers Yuqing, Hangong, and Lushi were all illustrious.

sentences.zh: 虞卿至工部侍郎、京兆尹，生堪，為太子少師。

translations.literal: Yuqing reached Vice Minister of Works and Metropolitan Governor and begot Kan, who was Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing rose to Vice Minister of Works and Metropolitan Governor and begot Kan, Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 堪生承休，昭宗朝，以兵部員外郎使吳越，會楊行密據淮甸，絕其歸路，因留浙中。

translations.literal: Kan begot Chenxiu, who in the Zhaozong reign, as Vice Director of War, was sent as envoy to Wu and Yue; Yang Xingmi held the Huai region and cut off his return route, and therefore he remained in Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Kan begot Chenxiu, who under Emperor Zhaozong was sent as Vice Director of War to Wu and Yue. Yang Xingmi held the Huai region and cut his return; he remained in Zhe.

sentences.zh: 承休生岩，即覃祖也，署為鎮海軍節度副使，奏領春州刺史。

translations.literal: Chenxiu begot Yan, Tan's grandfather; he was appointed by title military training vice commissioner and memorialized to hold the prefecture of Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Chenxiu begot Yan, Tan's grandfather, appointed by title as military training vice commissioner and memorialized as prefect of Chun.

sentences.zh: 岩生郁，早卒。

translations.literal: Yan begot Yu, who died young.
translations.idiomatic: Yan begot Yu, who died young.

sentences.zh: 覃少獻書於嗣王俶，俶私署著作佐郎，從俶歸朝，為禹城尉。

translations.literal: Tan in youth presented writings to the heir King Shu; Shu privately appointed him Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation. Following Shu on his return to court he was made warden of Yucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Tan presented writings to heir King Shu, who privately made him Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation. Following Shu to court he became warden of Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年，舉進士擢第，授徐州觀察推官，改著作佐郎、知戎州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed investigating officer of Xuzhou observation commission, changed to Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation and made prefect of Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi, was made investigating officer of Xuzhou, then Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation and prefect of Rong.

sentences.zh: 再遷太常博士，使陝西，蠲逋負。

translations.literal: After two promotions he was Doctor of the Grand Temple and sent to Shaanxi to remit arrears.
translations.idiomatic: After two promotions he was Doctor of the Grand Temple and sent to Shaanxi to remit tax arrears.

sentences.zh: 覃本名蟫，至是，太宗為改焉。

translations.literal: Tan's original name was Shan; at this time Emperor Taizong changed it for him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's original name was Shan; Taizong now changed it for him.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，轉屯田員外郎、同判壽州。

translations.literal: During Chunhua he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue for state farms and made concurrent administrator of Shou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunhua he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue for state farms and concurrent administrator of Shou.

sentences.zh: 巡撫使潘慎修上其政績，有詔嘉獎，就命知州事。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Pan Shenxiu memorialized his political achievements; there was an edict of commendation and he was appointed on the spot to administer the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Pan Shenxiu memorialized his achievements; an edict commended him and he was appointed on the spot to govern the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 數月，召還，未上道，會丁內艱，州民列狀乞留，轉運使以聞，有詔奪情。

translations.literal: Several months later he was summoned back; before he had set out on the road he entered mourning for a parent. The prefectural people submitted a collective petition begging to retain him; the transport commissioner reported it, and an edict ordered him to remain despite mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he was recalled, but before departing he entered mourning. The people petitioned to keep him; the transport commissioner reported it, and an edict ordered him to remain despite mourning.

sentences.zh: 時田重進為永興節度，選覃與林特同判軍府事，賜覃緋魚，仍賜御書曆，給以實奉。

translations.literal: At that time Tian Chongjin was military commissioner of Yongxing; he selected Tan together with Lin Te jointly to administer the military prefecture's affairs; Tan was granted crimson fish and still given an imperial calendar with full salary.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chongjin was then military commissioner of Yongxing; he chose Tan and Lin Te jointly to administer the prefecture. Tan was granted crimson fish and an imperial calendar with full salary.

sentences.zh: 重進不法，覃事多抗執，重進頗不悅，形於辭色。

translations.literal: Chongjin acted unlawfully; Tan often resisted him in affairs, and Chongjin was rather displeased, showing it in words and expression.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjin acted unlawfully; Tan often resisted him, and Chongjin showed his displeasure openly.

sentences.zh: 覃表求徙任，不許，就轉都官員外郎。

translations.literal: Tan memorialized begging transfer elsewhere; this was not granted, and he was transferred on the spot to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Tan begged transfer; it was denied, and he was made on the spot Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時討李繼遷，調發芻糧，覃、特皆以苛急促辦為務。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jiqian was being attacked; fodder and grain were mobilized; Tan and Te both made harsh urgency and rapid completion their task.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiqian was attacked, fodder and grain were mobilized; Tan and Te both drove collection with harsh urgency.

sentences.zh: 覃令鉗手，特令即械頸，雖衣冠舊族不免，人用怨嗟。

translations.literal: Tan ordered hand shackles, Te ordered immediate neck cangues—even old gentry families were not spared, and people murmured in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Tan ordered hand shackles and Te immediate neck cangues; even old gentry families were not spared, and resentment spread.

sentences.zh: 改職方員外郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，遷屯田郎中、三門發運使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue for state farms and made transport commissioner of Sanmen.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Xianping he was made Director in the Ministry of Revenue for state farms and transport commissioner of Sanmen.

sentences.zh: 呂蒙正在河南，薦其材，詔入判三司磨勘、憑由、理欠司。

translations.literal: Lü Mengzheng was in Henan and recommended his talent; an edict ordered him to enter as judge of the Three Departments' offices for audit, credentials, and arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Mengzheng in Henan recommended him; an edict ordered him to judge the Three Departments' audit, credentials, and arrears offices.

sentences.zh: 四年春，旱，覃上言：「古之用刑，皆避三統之月，漢舊章斷獄報重，盡三冬之月。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year there was drought; Tan memorialized: "In antiquity in applying punishments, all avoided the months of the three systems; the Han old statutes for reporting capital cases all ended in the three winter months.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year there was drought. Tan memorialized, "In antiquity punishments avoided the months of the three systems; Han statutes required capital cases to be concluded within the three winter months.

sentences.zh: 又唐太宗凡斷重刑日，敕減膳徹樂。

translations.literal: Moreover Emperor Taizong on every day he imposed capital punishment ordered reduced meals and music withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Taizong on every day of capital punishment ordered reduced meals and music withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 今春物方盛，時雨尚愆，輦轂之下，獄繫甚繁。

translations.literal: Now in spring things are flourishing, yet seasonal rain is still deficient; below the imperial carriage prisons are very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: This spring growth is at its height, yet rain is still scarce, and the prisons below the capital are overcrowded.

sentences.zh: 望詔有司，死罪未得論決，俟雨降，乃復常典。

translations.literal: I hope an edict may order the responsible offices that death sentences not yet decided should wait until rain falls, and then the regular statutes be resumed.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that offices be ordered not to decide death sentences until rain returns and the regular statutes resume.

sentences.zh: 仍望自今凡決重刑日，依唐故事，以彰至仁之德。」

translations.literal: I also hope that from now on, on every day capital punishment is imposed, the Tang precedent should be followed to display the utmost benevolent virtue."
translations.idiomatic: I also ask that hereafter, on every day of capital punishment, Tang precedent be followed to display the utmost benevolence."

sentences.zh: 嘗獻《時務策》五篇：一曰禦戎，二曰用兵，三曰為政，四曰選賢，五曰刑罰。

translations.literal: He once presented five chapters of "Policies for the Times": first, defending against barbarians; second, employing troops; third, governing; fourth, selecting the worthy; fifth, punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He once presented five essays on policies of the times: defending the frontier, employing troops, governing, selecting the worthy, and punishments.

sentences.zh: 文多不載。

translations.literal: The text is mostly not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the text is not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 明年，權同知貢舉，出為陝西轉運使，賜金紫。

translations.literal: The next year he was provisionally made concurrent supervisor of the examinations, went out as transport commissioner of Shaanxi, and was granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he provisionally supervised the examinations, was posted as transport commissioner of Shaanxi, and granted gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 會邊臣言繼遷死，願乘此時深入致討。

translations.literal: It happened that border officials reported that Jiqian had died and wished to take this opportunity to advance deep and launch punitive action.
translations.idiomatic: Border officials reported that Jiqian had died and urged a deep punitive campaign while the moment lasted.

sentences.zh: 覃建議：「伐喪非禮，且其子尚在，當為之備。

translations.literal: Tan memorialized: "Attacking during mourning is not ritual propriety, and moreover his son is still alive—we should prepare against him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan argued, "Attacking during mourning is unseemly, and his son still lives—we must prepare.

sentences.zh: 請詔邊臣謹守疆候，毋得輕舉，俟其眾叛親離，則亡無日矣。」

translations.literal: I beg an edict to border officials strictly to guard the frontier passes and not act rashly; wait until his followers rebel and kin desert him, and extinction will come in no long time."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that border officials guard the passes and not act rashly until followers rebel and kin desert him—then extinction will follow."

sentences.zh: 時西鄙屯兵，調役甚繁，副使朱台符務有為，而覃務循舊，且言邊事不宜更張。

translations.literal: At that time troops were stationed on the western border and corvée was very heavy; Vice Commissioner Zhu Taifu strove for achievement, while Tan strove to follow precedent and added border affairs should not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Troops massed on the western border and corvée was heavy. Vice Commissioner Zhu Taifu pushed innovation while Tan clung to precedent and said border affairs should not be changed.

sentences.zh: 初，寇準知青州，台符為通判。

translations.literal: Earlier Kou Zhun governed Qing Prefecture and Taifu was vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Kou Zhun governed Qing and Taifu was his vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 至是，準作相，覃意台符憑恃僚舊，密以上聞。

translations.literal: At this time Zhun became chief minister; Tan suspected Taifu relied on old staff ties and secretly reported this to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhun became chief minister, Tan suspected Taifu relied on old ties and secretly reported it.

sentences.zh: 坐不協，徙知隨州。

translations.literal: For lack of harmony he was transferred to govern Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: For lack of harmony he was transferred to Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 王超節制漢東，覃移唐州。

translations.literal: Wang Chao commanded Handong; Tan was transferred to Tang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chao commanded Handong; Tan was transferred to Tang.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，召歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingde he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 屬河北兵革之後，命覃詣澶、濱、棣、德、博州巡撫振給之。

translations.literal: It happened after warfare on the Hebei front; Tan was ordered to go to Chan, Bin, Di, De, and Bo prefectures to pacify and provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: After warfare on the Hebei front he was sent to Chan, Bin, Di, De, and Bo to pacify and provide relief.

sentences.zh: 出知潭州，王師討宜賊，軍須多出長沙，曹利用以聞，詔書褒勞，加刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Tan Prefecture; when the imperial army attacked the Yi bandits, military supplies mostly issued from Changsha; Cao Liyong reported this, and an edict commended his labors and gave him the additional title of Director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as prefect of Tan, he supplied the campaign against the Yi rebels from Changsha. Cao Liyong reported this; an edict commended him and made him Director in Punishments.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，代馮亮為淮南、江浙、荊湖制置發運使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu he replaced Feng Liang as commissioner for provisioning transport on Huainan, Jiang-Zhe, and Jing-Hu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu he replaced Feng Liang as provisioning transport commissioner for Huainan, Jiang-Zhe, and Jing-Hu.

sentences.zh: 月餘，改太常少卿、直昭文館、知廣州。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was changed to Vice Minister of Rites, Direct Academician, and made prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was made Vice Minister of Rites, Direct Academician, and prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 覃勤於吏事，所至以幹濟稱。

translations.literal: Tan was diligent in administrative affairs; wherever he went he was known for capable accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was diligent in office and known for capable accomplishment wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 南海有蕃舶之利，前後牧守或致謗議，惟覃以廉著，遠人便之。

translations.literal: The Southern Sea had profit from foreign merchant ships; former prefects and defenders often invited censure, but only Tan was known for integrity, and distant peoples found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The southern sea brought profit from foreign shipping; earlier governors often drew censure, but only Tan was known for integrity, to the comfort of distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 加右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Right Remonstrating Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Remonstrating Grandee.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 遣其長子奉禮郎文友乘傳赴喪，詔本州護柩還其家，官給所費。

translations.literal: His eldest son Gentleman for Court Ceremony Wenyou was sent by post relay to attend the funeral; an edict ordered the prefecture to escort the coffin home and supply the expenses.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Wenyou was sent by post to mourn; an edict ordered the prefecture to escort the coffin home at state expense.

sentences.zh: 錄其次子文敏為揚州司士參軍。

translations.literal: His second son Wenmin was entered as judicial administrator of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Wenmin was entered as judicial administrator of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 覃從弟蛻及從子侃、傅，並登進士第。

translations.literal: Tan's younger cousin Tui and nephews Kan and Fu all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's cousin Tui and nephews Kan and Fu all passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 蛻官司封員外郎，侃後名大雅，自有傳。

translations.literal: Tui held office as Vice Director in the Ministry of Provisions; Kan later named Daya has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Tui was Vice Director in the Ministry of Provisions; Kan, later named Daya, has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 陳世卿

translations.literal: Chen Shiqing
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shiqing

sentences.zh: 陳世卿，字光遠，南劍人。

translations.literal: Chen Shiqing, courtesy name Guangyuan, was a native of Nanjian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shiqing, whose courtesy name was Guangyuan, came from Nanjian.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，登進士第，解褐衡州推官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he passed the jinshi examination; on leaving office he was made investigating officer of Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he passed the jinshi and entered service as investigating officer of Heng.

sentences.zh: 再調東川節度推官。

translations.literal: After a second transfer he was investigating officer of the Dongchuan military commission.
translations.idiomatic: After a second transfer he was investigating officer of the Dongchuan military commission.

sentences.zh: 會李順寇兩川，知州張雍以州兵馬為數部，使官分領。

translations.literal: When Li Shun raided the two Sichuan circuits, Prefect Zhang Yong divided the prefectural troops into several sections and had officials command each.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shun raided Sichuan, Prefect Zhang Yong divided the garrison into sections under separate officers.

sentences.zh: 世卿素善射，當城一面，親射中數百人。

translations.literal: Shiqing was by nature skilled at archery; on the face of the wall he commanded he personally shot and hit several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at archery, Shiqing commanded one wall and personally shot down several hundred men.

sentences.zh: 賊寢盛，同幕皆謀圖全計。

translations.literal: The bandits gradually grew strong; colleagues on the staff all plotted plans for self-preservation.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels grew stronger, staff colleagues all plotted escape.

sentences.zh: 世卿正色曰：「食君祿，當委身報國，奈何欲避難為他圖耶？」

translations.literal: Shiqing said sternly: "We eat the ruler's salary—should we not devote our persons to repay the state? How can you wish to flee hardship and make other plans?"
translations.idiomatic: Shiqing said sternly, "We eat the ruler's salary—should we not give our lives for the state? How can you seek escape?"

sentences.zh: 亟出白雍曰：「此徒皆懦儒，存之適足惑眾，不若遣出求援。」

translations.literal: He immediately went out and told Yong: "These men are all cowardly scholars; keeping them will only confuse the troops—better send them out to seek relief."
translations.idiomatic: He told Yong at once, "These are cowards; keeping them will confuse the troops—send them out for relief."

sentences.zh: 雍從之。

translations.literal: Yong followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Yong agreed.

sentences.zh: 賊既引去，世卿適丁外艱，雍表其材，詔追出視事，就改掌書記。

translations.literal: After the bandits had withdrawn, Shiqing happened to enter mourning for his father; Yong memorialized his talent, and an edict ordered him recalled to resume office and he was changed on the spot to secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels withdrew Shiqing entered mourning for his father. Yong memorialized his talent; an edict recalled him and made him secretary.

sentences.zh: 凡七年，歸朝，為秘書郎，遷太常丞、知新安縣。

translations.literal: Altogether seven years; he returned to court as Secretary, was transferred to Vice Director of the Grand Temple and made prefect of Xin'an County.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years in all; he returned as Secretary, then Vice Director of the Grand Temple and prefect of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 或薦其堪任憲臺，即召歸，會張鏗出知廣州，表為通判。

translations.literal: Someone recommended him as fit for the Censorate; he was immediately summoned back, but it happened that Zhang Keng went out as prefect of Guangzhou and memorialized him as vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for the censorate, he was recalled, but Zhang Keng was going to Guangzhou and took him as vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 將行，召見，賜緋，加太常博士。

translations.literal: Before departing he was summoned for audience, granted crimson robes, and given the additional title of Doctor of the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing he was summoned, granted crimson robes, and made Doctor of the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 景德初，徙知建州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he was transferred to govern Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Jingde he was transferred to Jian.

sentences.zh: 真宗知其材幹，逾月，授福轉建運使，規畫南劍州安仁等銀場，歲增課羨，詔獎之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong knew his capability; after more than a month he was made transport commissioner of Fu and Jian and planned the Anren and other silver mines in Nanjian; yearly tax surplus increased, and an edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong knew his ability; a month later he was made transport commissioner of Fu and Jian, planned the Anren silver mines in Nanjian, increased yearly revenue, and won an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 俄代姚鉉為兩浙路轉運使，歷祠部員外郎，判三司三勾院。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Yao Xian as transport commissioner of the two Zhe circuits, successively served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, and judged the Three Departments' three audit offices.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he replaced Yao Xian as transport commissioner for the two Zhe circuits, rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, and judged the three audit offices.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符四年，改度支員外郎，出為荊湖北路轉運使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was changed to Vice Director of Revenue and went out as transport commissioner of Jinghu North Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was made Vice Director of Revenue and transport commissioner of Jinghu North Circuit.

sentences.zh: 屬澧州慈利縣下溪等四州蠻人侵縣境地四百餘里，朝命世卿與閤門祗候史方、知澧州劉仁霸同領兵討之，遂還所侵地，標正經界，取其要領，又令納所掠漢口千餘，復置澧川、武口等砦以控制之，自是平定，有詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: It happened that the Xi barbarians of Xiaxi and three other districts in Cili County of Li Prefecture invaded more than four hundred li of county territory; the court ordered Shiqing together with Palace Attendant Shi Fang and Prefect Liu Renba jointly to lead troops to attack them. They recovered the invaded land, marked the correct boundaries, took their leaders, and also ordered them to surrender more than a thousand Han people they had seized; Fuchuan, Wukou, and other stockades were re-established to control them. From this peace was settled, and there was an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi tribes of Xiaxi and three other districts in Cili invaded more than four hundred li of county land, Shiqing was ordered with Palace Attendant Shi Fang and Prefect Liu Renba to attack them. They recovered the land, fixed boundaries, took leaders, recovered more than a thousand captive Han people, and re-established stockades at Fuchuan and Wukou. Peace followed and an edict commended them.

sentences.zh: 還朝，屢述溪洞利害。

translations.literal: On returning to court he repeatedly set forth the advantages and harms of the stream grottoes.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he repeatedly explained the interests of the stream grottoes.

sentences.zh: 召對，真宗器其材，復自言願效用於煩劇。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, Zhenzong valued his talent; he again spoke himself wishing to serve in urgent and complex duties.
translations.idiomatic: At audience Zhenzong valued his talent; he again asked to serve in demanding posts.

sentences.zh: 會邵曄知廣州，被疾，乃授世卿秘書少監代之，加賜金紫。

translations.literal: It happened that Shao Ye governed Guangzhou and fell ill; he was therefore given Shiqing as Vice Director of the Secretariat to replace him, with additional grant of gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao Ye governed Guangzhou and fell ill, Shiqing was made Vice Director of the Secretariat to replace him, with gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 郡有計口買鹽之制，人多不便，至，即奏除之。

translations.literal: The prefecture had a system of purchasing salt by head count, which many found inconvenient; when he arrived he immediately memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture taxed salt by head count, which many resented; on arrival he memorialized to abolish it.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 錄其子南安主簿儼為太祝。

translations.literal: His son Yan, registrar of Nan'an, was entered as Supplicator of the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan, registrar of Nan'an, was entered as Supplicator of the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 李若拙

translations.literal: Li Ruozhuo
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruozhuo

sentences.zh: 李若拙，字藏用，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Li Ruozhuo, courtesy name Zangyong, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruozhuo, whose courtesy name was Zangyong, came from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父光贊，貝冀觀察判官。

translations.literal: His father Guangzan was investigating officer of the Bei-Ji observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guangzan was investigating officer of the Bei-Ji observation commission.

sentences.zh: 若拙初以蔭補太廟齋郎，復舉拔萃，授大名府戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: Ruozhuo at first entered office by yin privilege as Acolyte of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; he again passed the extraordinary selection and was appointed revenue administrator of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ruozhuo first entered by yin as Acolyte of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, then passed the extraordinary selection and became revenue administrator of Daming.

sentences.zh: 時符彥卿在鎮，光贊居幕下，若拙得以就養。

translations.literal: At that time Fu Yanqing was in the prefecture and Guangzan was on his staff; Ruozhuo was therefore able to support his father nearby.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing then held the prefecture and Guangzan served on his staff, so Ruozhuo could support his father nearby.

sentences.zh: 俄又舉進士，王祐典貢舉，擢上第，授密州防禦推官。

translations.literal: Before long he again passed the jinshi examination; Wang You supervised the examinations, selected him for top rank, and appointed him investigating officer of Mizhou defense commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he passed the jinshi; Wang You supervised the examinations, placed him first, and made him investigating officer of Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 登賢良方正直言極諫科，太祖嘉其敏贍，改著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He passed the direct and blunt remonstrance examination for the worthy and eminent; Emperor Taizu commended his sharpness and efficiency and changed him to Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examination for worthy and eminent direct remonstrance; Taizu commended his sharpness and made him Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation.

sentences.zh: 故事，制策中選者除拾遺、補闕。

translations.literal: By precedent, those selected in the policy examination were made remembrancers and remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, policy examination winners were made remembrancers and remonstrators.

sentences.zh: 若拙以恩例不及，上書自陳，執政惡之，出監商州坑冶。

translations.literal: Ruozhuo was not covered by the favor precedent; he memorialized on his own behalf; the chief ministers disliked this and sent him out to supervise Shangzhou mining.
translations.idiomatic: Ruozhuo was excluded by the favor rule; he memorialized for himself; the chief ministers disliked it and sent him to supervise Shangzhou mining.

sentences.zh: 遷太子左贊善大夫，以官稱與父名同，辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Assistant in the Eastern Palace; because the office title was the same as his father's name, he declined, but this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Left Assistant in the Eastern Palace, he declined because the title matched his father's name, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，知乾州，會李飛雄詐乘驛稱詔使，事敗伏法。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he governed Qian Prefecture; it happened that Li Feixiong falsely rode post relay claiming to be an edict envoy; when the affair was exposed he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he governed Qian. Li Feixiong falsely rode post relay claiming to be an edict envoy; exposed, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 太宗以若拙與飛雄父若愚連名，疑其昆弟，命殿直盧令珣即捕繫州獄，乃與若愚同宗，通家非親，不知其謀，猶坐削籍流海島。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, because Ruozhuo shared the name character with Feixiong's father Ruoyu, suspected they were brothers; he ordered Palace Direct Lu Lingxun immediately to arrest and imprison him in the prefectural prison. They were of the same clan as Ruoyu, families in contact but not kin, and did not know the plot—yet he was still punished by removal from the register and exile to the sea islands.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, seeing Ruozhuo shared a name character with Feixiong's father Ruoyu, suspected kinship and ordered Lu Lingxun to arrest him. They were clan kin of Ruoyu, not close family, and knew nothing—yet Ruozhuo was struck from the register and exiled to the islands.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，起授衛尉寺丞、知隴州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was raised and appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and made prefect of Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was raised to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and prefect of Long.

sentences.zh: 四年，復舊官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he recovered his original office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he recovered his original rank.

sentences.zh: 以政聞，超授監察御史、通判泰州。

translations.literal: Because of his governance he was specially promoted to Supervisory Censor and made vice commissioner of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his governance he was made Supervisory Censor and vice commissioner of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 同帥宋偓年老政弛，又徙若拙通判焉。

translations.literal: Commander Song Wo was old and his government slackened; Ruozhuo was again transferred as vice commissioner there.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Song Wo was elderly and slack; Ruozhuo was again made vice commissioner there.

sentences.zh: 未幾，御史中丞滕中正薦之，召歸臺。

translations.literal: Before long Vice Censor-in-Chief Teng Zhongzheng recommended him and he was summoned back to the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Teng Zhongzheng recommended him and he returned to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 頃之，改右補闕。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 時諸王出閣，若拙獻頌稱旨，召見，賜緋魚，同勾當河東轉運兼雲、應等八州事。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial princes left the palace; Ruozhuo presented a eulogy that pleased the emperor; he was summoned for audience, granted crimson fish, and jointly handled Hedong transport together with Yun, Ying, and eight other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the princes left the palace Ruozhuo presented a eulogy that pleased the emperor; summoned, he was granted crimson fish and jointly handled Hedong transport with Yun, Ying, and eight other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣闕言邊事，太宗嘉之。

translations.literal: Once he memorialized at court on border affairs and Taizong commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized on border affairs and Taizong commended him.

sentences.zh: 又同掌水陸發運司。

translations.literal: He also jointly administered the water and land transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: He also jointly administered water and land transport.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，假秘書監使交州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he was provisionally made Vice Director of the Secretariat as envoy to Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he was provisionally made Vice Director of the Secretariat and envoy to Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，黎桓制度逾僭，若拙既入境，即遣左右戒以臣禮，繇是桓聽命，拜詔盡恭。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Huan's institutions had exceeded proper rank; after Ruozhuo entered the territory he immediately sent attendants to admonish him with the ritual of subject, and from this Huan obeyed orders and received the patent with full respect.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan had exceeded proper rank; on entering the territory Ruozhuo admonished him to observe subject ritual, and Huan obeyed and received the patent respectfully.

sentences.zh: 燕饗日，以奇貨異物列於前，若拙一不留眄。

translations.literal: On the day of the banquet rare goods and exotic objects were set before him; Ruozhuo did not glance at them once.
translations.idiomatic: At the banquet rare goods were displayed; Ruozhuo never glanced at them.

sentences.zh: 取先陷蠻使鄧君辯以歸，禮幣外，不受其私覿。

translations.literal: He took the former captive envoy Deng Junbian and returned; apart from ritual gifts he accepted no private audience gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He brought back the former captive envoy Deng Junbian and accepted no gifts beyond ritual tribute.

sentences.zh: 使還，上謂其不辱命。

translations.literal: When the mission returned the emperor said he had not disgraced his commission.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the emperor said he had not disgraced his commission.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人，充鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant on the Emperor's Diary and made Salt and Iron judge.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Attendant on the Emperor's Diary and Salt and Iron judge.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，出為兩浙轉運使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he went out as transport commissioner of the two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua he was transport commissioner of the two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇邊，改職方員外郎，徙河北路，賜金紫。

translations.literal: When the Khitan raided the border he was changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and transferred to Hebei Circuit, and was granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided he was made Vice Director in Works, transferred to Hebei, and granted gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 五年，直昭文館，遷主客郎中、江南轉運使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was Direct Academician and transferred to Director in the Ministry of Rites and transport commissioner of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was Direct Academician, then Director in the Ministry of Rites and transport commissioner of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 若拙質狀魁偉，尚氣有幹才，然臨事太緩。

translations.literal: Ruozhuo was by nature large and imposing, valued integrity and had capability, yet in affairs he was too slow.
translations.idiomatic: Ruozhuo was large and imposing, spirited and capable, yet too slow in action.

sentences.zh: 宰相以為言，罷使知涇州。

translations.literal: The chief ministers spoke of this and he was dismissed from his commission and made prefect of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers spoke of this; he was dismissed as commissioner and made prefect of Jing.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，黎桓復侵南鄙，又詔若拙充使，至，則桓復稟命。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao, Li Huan again invaded the southern border; Ruozhuo was again ordered as envoy; when he arrived Huan again obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao Huan again invaded the south; Ruozhuo was again envoy, and Huan again submitted.

sentences.zh: 使還，真宗嗣位，召見慰問，進秩金部郎中。

translations.literal: When the mission returned Zhenzong had succeeded; he was summoned for audience and comforted, and promoted in rank to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On return Zhenzong had succeeded; summoned and comforted, he was promoted to Director in Revenue.

sentences.zh: 召試學士院，改兵部郎中，充史館修撰，俄知制誥。

translations.literal: Summoned to examination in the Academy, he was changed to Director in the Ministry of War, made compiler of the Historiography Institute, and soon Drafter of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Examined in the Academy, he was made Director in War, compiler of the Historiography Institute, and soon Drafter of Edicts.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，同知貢舉，被疾，改右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was made concurrent supervisor of the examinations; when he fell ill he was changed to Right Remonstrating Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Xianping he supervised the examinations; when ill he was made Right Remonstrating Grandee.

sentences.zh: 車駕北巡，判留司御史臺。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured the north he was assigned to judge the capital censorate while the emperor was away.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the north he judged the capital censorate in his absence.

sentences.zh: 明年，使河朔按邊事，知昇、貝二州。

translations.literal: The next year he was envoy to Hebei to inspect border affairs and governed Sheng and Bei prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he inspected the Hebei border and governed Sheng and Bei.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子繹。

translations.literal: Son Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yi.

sentences.zh: 子 繹

translations.literal: Son Yi
translations.idiomatic: Son Yi

sentences.zh: 繹，字縱之，幼謹愿自修。

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Zongzhi, in youth was cautious and cultivated himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, whose courtesy name was Zongzhi, was cautious and self-cultivating from youth.

sentences.zh: 初，以父使交阯有勞，補太廟齋郎，改太常寺太祝。

translations.literal: At first, because his father as envoy to Jiaozhi had merit, he was appointed Acolyte of the Imperial Ancestral Temple by yin and changed to Supplicator of the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father's mission to Jiaozhi had merit, he entered by yin as Acolyte of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, then became Supplicator of the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 舉進士中第，除將作監丞。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was made Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and was made Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書屯田員外郎、知華州。

translations.literal: After repeated promotions he was Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue for state farms and made prefect of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated promotions he was Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue for state farms and prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 蒲城民李蘊訴人盜其從子亡去，繹問曰：「若有仇耶？」

translations.literal: A man of Pucheng, Li Yun, sued that someone had stolen his nephew and the nephew had disappeared; Yi asked: "If there were an enemy?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun of Pucheng sued that someone had stolen his nephew, who had vanished. Yi asked, "Was there an enemy?"

sentences.zh: 曰：無有。」

translations.literal: He said: "There was none."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "None."

sentences.zh: 曰：「有失亡邪？」

translations.literal: He said: "If there were a loss or disappearance?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked, "Was there a loss or disappearance?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「無有。」

translations.literal: He said: "There was none."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "None."

sentences.zh: 繹揮蘊去，因密刺蘊，蘊有陰罪，侄覺之，懼事暴，殺之以滅口，遂收蘊致法。

translations.literal: Yi dismissed Yun and therefore secretly investigated Yun; Yun had hidden crimes, and the nephew discovered them, feared exposure, killed him to silence him, and then Yi arrested Yun and brought him to law.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent Yun away and secretly investigated him. Yun had hidden crimes; the nephew discovered them, killed Yun to silence him, and Yi arrested Yun and brought him to justice.

sentences.zh: 擢提點河北刑獄，權知貝州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervise penal affairs on Hebei and given provisional charge of Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervise penal affairs on Hebei and given provisional charge of Bei.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，繹為酒務，市民薪草溢常數，餓者皆以樵采自給，得不死，官入亦數倍。

translations.literal: In a drought year Yi was in charge of the wine monopoly; townspeople's firewood and grass exceeded the usual quota, and the hungry all supported themselves by gathering fuel and did not die; government revenue also increased several fold.
translations.idiomatic: In a drought year, as wine monopoly officer he let townspeople exceed the usual quota for firewood and grass; the hungry gathered fuel and survived, and government revenue also multiplied.

sentences.zh: 邊民歲輸防城火牛草十餘萬，委積久，輒腐敗，繹奏罷之。

translations.literal: Border people yearly delivered more than a hundred thousand bundles of fire-oxen grass for frontier defense; piled up long it always rotted; Yi memorialized to abolish this.
translations.idiomatic: Border people yearly delivered more than a hundred thousand bundles of frontier fire-cattle grass; stored long it rotted, and Yi memorialized to abolish the levy.

sentences.zh: 三遷本曹郎中，為利州路轉運使。

translations.literal: After three promotions he was Director in that bureau and made transport commissioner of Lizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he was director of that bureau and transport commissioner of Lizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 河北經費不支，仁宗問誰可任者，參知政事薛奎薦繹，遂徙河北。

translations.literal: Hebei expenses could not be met; Emperor Renzong asked who could take the post; Vice Director of the Secretariat Xue Kui recommended Yi, and he was therefore transferred to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei expenses could not be met; Renzong asked who could serve; Vice Director Xue Kui recommended Yi, and he was transferred to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 進刑部郎中、直史館、知延州，改兵部，為江淮制置發運使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Punishments, Direct Academician, and made prefect of Yan Prefecture; changed to War, and made commissioner for provisioning transport on Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director in Punishments, Direct Academician, and prefect of Yan, then War, and provisioning transport commissioner for Jiang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 內出絹五十萬匹，責貿於東南。

translations.literal: From the palace five hundred thousand bolts of silk were issued with orders to trade them in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: The palace issued five hundred thousand bolts of silk to be traded in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 繹曰：「百姓饑，不宜重擾。」

translations.literal: Yi said: "The people are hungry—it is not fitting to burden them further."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The people are hungry—it is wrong to burden them further."

sentences.zh: 輒奏罷之。

translations.literal: He immediately memorialized to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized at once to stop it.

sentences.zh: 甫半年，漕課視常歲增五之一。

translations.literal: In barely half a year transport revenue increased by one-fifth over an ordinary year.
translations.idiomatic: In half a year transport revenue rose one-fifth above an ordinary year.

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿，再知延州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and again made prefect of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of Rites and again prefect of Yan.

sentences.zh: 繹所至頗稱治，自以久宦在外，意不自得，作《五知先生傳》，謂知時、知難、知命、知退、知足也。

translations.literal: Wherever Yi went he was rather praised for good governance; because he had long served outside he was not content in mind and composed "Biography of the Master of Five Knowings," meaning knowing the times, knowing difficulty, knowing fate, knowing withdrawal, and knowing sufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Yi went he won praise for governance, but long service abroad left him dissatisfied; he wrote "Biography of the Master of Five Knowings"—knowing the times, difficulty, fate, withdrawal, and sufficiency.

sentences.zh: 嘗兩知鳳翔府，至是，又徙鳳翔。

translations.literal: He twice governed Fengxiang Prefecture; at this time he was again transferred to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He had twice governed Fengxiang and was now transferred there again.

sentences.zh: 尋為右諫議大夫，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Right Remonstrating Grandee and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Right Remonstrating Grandee and died.

sentences.zh: 陳知微

translations.literal: Chen Zhiwei
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhiwei

sentences.zh: 陳知微，字希顏，高郵人。

translations.literal: Chen Zhiwei, courtesy name Xiyan, was a native of Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhiwei, whose courtesy name was Xiyan, came from Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 咸平五年，進士甲科，解褐將作監丞、通判歙州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianping he passed the jinshi examination in the top class; on leaving office he was made Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and vice commissioner of She Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianping he passed the jinshi in the top class and entered service as Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and vice commissioner of She.

sentences.zh: 擢為著作佐郎、直史館，俄充三司戶部判官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation and Direct Academician; soon he was made judge of the Revenue Bureau in the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Assistant in the Bureau of Compilation and Direct Academician, then judge of the Revenue Bureau in the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 奉使契丹，遷太常博士、判三司都磨勘司，再為戶部判官，出為京東轉運副使，奏還東平監所侵民田六百八十家。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to the Khitan, he was transferred to Doctor of the Grand Temple and judge of the Three Departments Audit Office; again Revenue judge; went out as Vice Transport Commissioner of Jingdong and memorialized returning more than six hundred and eighty households' fields invaded by the Dongping Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: As envoy to the Khitan he was made Doctor of the Grand Temple and judge of the Three Departments Audit Office, then again Revenue judge, then Vice Transport Commissioner of Jingdong, where he memorialized returning six hundred and eighty households' fields seized by the Dongping Directorate.

sentences.zh: 又決古廣濟河通運路，罷夾黃河，歲減夫役數萬計。

translations.literal: He also opened the ancient Guangji River to clear the transport route and abolished the Yellow River cutoff, yearly reducing corvée by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He reopened the ancient Guangji River for transport and abolished the Yellow River cutoff, saving tens of thousands of corvée days yearly.

sentences.zh: 遷右司諫，徙荊湖南路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Remonstrator of the Secretariat and made transport commissioner of Hunan South Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Remonstrator of the Secretariat and transport commissioner of Hunan South Circuit.

sentences.zh: 召還，拜比部員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: Summoned back, he was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Drafter of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Drafter of Edicts.

sentences.zh: 淮南饑，遣知微巡撫，所至按視儲糧，察諸官吏能否。

translations.literal: Huainan suffered famine; he was sent to pacify and comfort; wherever he went he inspected stored grain and examined whether officials were capable.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan suffered famine he was sent to inspect; wherever he went he checked stored grain and officials' competence.

sentences.zh: 使還，判吏部銓，兼刑部。

translations.literal: When the mission returned he judged the Ministry of Personnel's selection board concurrently with Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: On return he judged the Ministry of Personnel's selection board and concurrently Punishments.

sentences.zh: 知微祠藻雖無奇采，而平雅適用。

translations.literal: Zhiwei's ritual compositions, though without extraordinary color, were level and elegant and fit for use.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwei's ritual compositions lacked flash but were level, elegant, and serviceable.

sentences.zh: 一日，進改群官，除目紛委，適當知微次直，思亦敏速。

translations.literal: One day, when advancing group appointments, the appointment documents were numerous and happened to fall on Zhiwei's turn on duty; his thinking was also sharp and swift.
translations.idiomatic: One day, when many appointments were issued, they fell on Zhiwei's duty shift; his mind was sharp and swift.

sentences.zh: 又判司農寺，糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: He also judged the Directorate of Agriculture and investigated capital penal cases.
translations.idiomatic: He also judged the Directorate of Agriculture and investigated capital penal cases.

sentences.zh: 天禧二年，加玉清昭應宮判官，俄以疾聞，真宗遣中貴挾太醫往視之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxi he was given the additional post of judge of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace; soon his illness was reported; Zhenzong sent a palace attendant with imperial physicians to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianxi he was made judge of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace; when illness was reported Zhenzong sent a palace attendant with imperial physicians.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty.

sentences.zh: 錄其子舜卿為太常奉禮郎，給奉終喪，又假官船載其柩還鄉里。

translations.literal: His son Shunqing was entered as Gentleman for Court Ceremony of the Grand Temple, given stipends through mourning, and also lent an official boat to carry his coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shunqing was entered as Gentleman for Court Ceremony of the Grand Temple, given stipends through mourning, and lent an official boat to carry the coffin home.

sentences.zh: 知微儀狀甚偉，沉厚有材幹，不務察，時人許其處劇，惜其母老不克終養。

translations.literal: Zhiwei's bearing was very imposing, deep and substantial with capability; he did not strive for scrutiny, and contemporaries approved his handling of urgent business, regretting that his mother was old and he could not complete final nurturing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwei was imposing and capable, not given to petty scrutiny; contemporaries approved his handling of demanding duties, regretting that his aged mother kept him from completing filial nurturing.

sentences.zh: 有集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in thirty chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in thirty chapters.

sentences.zh: 子堯卿，大中祥符五年，進士及第。

translations.literal: His son Yaoqing passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yaoqing passed the jinshi in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 論曰：維岳明習吏事，才足以治劇，而能曲全法掾，其仁恕藹然。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Weiyue was well versed in administrative affairs, his talent sufficient for urgent business, and yet able tactfully to preserve the legal clerk—his benevolence and forbearance were genial.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Weiyue knew administration thoroughly, had talent for demanding duties, and could tactfully spare the legal clerk—his benevolence was evident.

sentences.zh: 雍雖素稱鄙吝，而勤恪清幹，觀其捍守，亦可見矣。

translations.literal: Although Yong was always called mean and stingy, he was diligent, respectful, and clear in efficiency; viewing his stout defense, this too can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yong was called mean, he was diligent and efficient; his stout defense shows it.

sentences.zh: 儼務進瀆貨，廷式傾險忌刻，自不容於清議。

translations.literal: Yan strove for advancement and accepted bribes; Tingshi was treacherous and jealous—by themselves they could not stand in pure opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Yan pursued advancement through bribes; Tingshi was treacherous and jealous—neither could stand in honest opinion.

sentences.zh: 若琰、摶經制漕運有方，策之處事精詳，治跡昭著，覃之律身廉潔，兼勤吏事，世卿之安遠，若拙之專對，皆為時論所許。

translations.literal: As for Yan and Tuan, they had methods for managing transport; Ce's affairs were precise, his traces of governance illustrious; Tan regulated himself with integrity and was also diligent in office; Shiqing's pacification of the distant, Ruozhuo's exclusive audience—all were approved in opinion of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Tuan managed transport well; Ce was precise and left a clear record; Tan was incorruptible and diligent; Shiqing pacified the distant and Ruozhuo acquitted himself at court—all won contemporary approval.

sentences.zh: 繹以謹愿，克世其家，知微敦實有材幹，不辱其職，亦可尚也。

translations.literal: Yi by caution and cultivation continued his family line; Zhiwei was solid and capable and did not disgrace his post—these too are to be respected.
translations.idiomatic: Yi continued the family through caution; Zhiwei was solid and capable and did not disgrace his office—both are worthy of respect.

sentences.zh: 至若王陟以謹幹稱，而取士以謗致汙，惜哉！

translations.literal: As for Wang Zhi, he was praised for caution and efficiency, yet in selecting scholars he was stained by slander—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi was praised for caution and efficiency, yet slander over selecting scholars stained him—alas!
